title: Feature/Bug: Math evaluation (eval) fails in position/size fields unless "px" suffix is manually deleted
author: Dillon3455
body:
**Description:**
When trying to use math formulas (e.g., 1080/2) in coordinate or size input fields, the evaluation fails if the px suffix is present.
If a user double-clicks the number to change it, the px part remains untouched. Typing an expression like 1080/2 px does not work, forcing the user to completely clear the field manually before typing the formula.
**Steps to Reproduce:**
1. Open VectorCraft (v1.1.0 Portable).
2. Select any object and go to an input field (like Position X/Y or Width/Height).
3. Double-click the numeric value so only the number is highlighted, leaving the px suffix intact.
4. Type a math expression (e.g., 1080/2) and press Enter.
5. Actual Result: The expression does not evaluate because of the trailing px. The user is forced to delete everything in the field to make it work.
**Expected Behavior:**
The input field should either:
• Automatically strip or ignore the px suffix when evaluating math expressions.
• Highlight the entire field (including px) on a double-click/focus, so it gets overwritten instantly.
**Environment:**
• VectorCraft Version: 1.1.0 Portable

title: Bug: Ctrl+Shift+V behaves identically to Ctrl+V instead of Performing "Paste in Place"
author: Dillon3455
body:
Description:
Currently, both Ctrl + V and Ctrl + Shift + V shortcuts share the same behavior. Instead of placing the copied object at its original coordinates (Paste in Place), Ctrl + Shift + V randomly offsets the object or places it arbitrarily, completely mirroring the default Ctrl + V action.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open VectorCraft (v1.1.0 Portable).
2. Create or select any object on the canvas.
3. Copy it using Ctrl + C.
4. Press Ctrl + Shift + V to paste it.
5. Actual Result: The object is pasted with an offset or in a random position, exactly like a regular Ctrl + V output. It does not match the original coordinates.
Expected Behavior:
• Ctrl + V: Pastes the object with a visual offset or centered to the viewport.
• Ctrl + Shift + V: Must perform a strict Paste in Place action, spawning the duplicated object at the exact same X/Y coordinates as the original source.
Environment:
• VectorCraft Version: 1.1.0 Portable

title: Bug: Saved files are missing file extension by default
author: Dillon3455
body:
Description:
When saving a new project (e.g., "Untitled-1"), the application creates a file without any file extension if the user doesn't manually type it into the filename field. This causes the operating system to recognize it as an unknown file type.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open VectorCraft (v1.1.0 Portable).
2. Create any object or shape on the canvas.
3. Press Ctrl + S (or go to File -> Save).
4. Leave the default name "Untitled-1" (or type a new name without manually adding an extension like .svg or .vcraft) and click Save.
5. Check the folder where the file was saved.
6. Actual Result: The file is saved literally as Untitled-1 with no extension at all. The OS cannot open it automatically.
Expected Behavior:
The application should automatically append the correct native file extension (e.g., .svg, .vcraft, or whatever format VectorCraft uses) to the file name upon saving.
Environment:
• VectorCraft Version: 1.1.0 Portable

title: Bug: Absolute rotation is applied destructively, discarding local object space and handles
author: Dillon3455
body:
Description:
Currently, entering a value in the rotation field (e.g., 45) behaves like a destructive matrix bake rather than setting a persistent property.
The application modifies the shape's raw vertices globally, resets the inspector's rotation value back to 0, and forces a global axis-aligned bounding box over it. This completely strips the object of its local coordinate system, making it impossible to see its actual angle or scale it along its local edges using side handles.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open VectorCraft (v1.1.0 Portable).
2. Create a rectangle and select it.
3. In the Inspector, type 45 in the rotation field and press Enter.
4. Observe the object and its transformation controls.
5. Actual Result: The shape rotates, but the inspector resets to 0. The transformation box remains global, and there are no local side handles to extend the rectangle's width or height along its new angle.
Expected Behavior:
Rotation should be a non-destructive local property. When an object is rotated:
• The inspector should display and retain the persistent angle (e.g., 45°).
• The bounding box and its resizing handles should rotate with the object, allowing local scaling along its axes.
Environment:
• VectorCraft Version: 1.1.0 Portable

title: Feature Request: Add an "Aspect Ratio Lock" (chain icon) for proportional scaling
author: Dillon3455
body:
Description:
Currently, there is no option to lock the aspect ratio when changing the dimensions (Width/Height) of an object in the inspector. Users are forced to manually calculate or guess the proportions when resizing shapes via input fields.
It would be extremely helpful to add a "chain" toggle button between the Width and Height input fields to link them together, ensuring proportional scaling.
Expected Behavior:
• When the link/chain button is disabled (unlocked): Width and Height can be changed independently (current behavior).
• When the link/chain button is enabled (locked): Changing the Width value automatically recalculates and updates the Height value proportionally (and vice versa) [health].
Environment:
• VectorCraft Version: 1.1.0 Portable

title: Bug: Hint bar shows macOS key names (Option, Cmd) on Windows and Linux
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
On Windows (and Linux), the hint bar at the bottom of the window uses macOS key names: **Option** instead of **Alt**, and **Cmd** instead of **Ctrl**. The menus already show the right names on Windows (e.g. `Ctrl+=`), so the hint bar disagrees with the rest of the app.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Run VectorCraft on Windows and open or create any document.
2. Select the Selection tool, then the Zoom, Rotate and Paintbrush tools, and read the hint bar each time.

**Actual result**
- Selection: "**Option+Drag** the object to duplicate"
- Shape tools: "**Option+Drag** from center"
- Zoom: "**Option+Click** to zoom out"
- Rotate / Reflect / Scale / Shear: "**Option+Click** for exact values"
- Every tool without its own hint (e.g. Paintbrush): "Press **Cmd+Shift+/** to search every command"

The Eyedropper hint already says "Alt+Click", so the hints aren't consistent with each other either.

**Expected result**
Alt and Ctrl on Windows and Linux (Option and Cmd on macOS), the same names the menus use.

**Screenshots**
Hint bar for four tools on Windows:

![Hint bar showing Option+Drag, Option+Click and Cmd+Shift+/ on Windows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/hint-bar-tools.png)

The View menu on the same machine shows Ctrl:

![View menu showing Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- on Windows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/view-menu-ctrl.png)

**Where it comes from**
`hint_for()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/chrome.rs` hard-codes the strings. The menus translate shortcut labels per platform (`crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`, around line 1808), but the hint bar doesn't go through that.

**Environment**
- VectorCraft built from `main` at 0c65fe7 (also in the v0.1.1 Windows portable release)
- Windows 11 Pro, 1600×900 at 100% scaling

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Chinese, Japanese and Korean text shows as missing-glyph boxes in the UI
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters show as empty boxes (missing glyphs) in the UI (confirmed in the Layers panel and document tabs), although the same text renders correctly on the canvas. Anyone who names layers or files in these scripts, or types text in them, sees boxes instead of names.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Create a document, pick the Type tool and type `Logo 标志 ロゴ 로고`.
2. Open the Layers panel.
3. Save the document as `标志设计.vectorcraft` and look at its tab.

**Actual result**
- The canvas renders the text correctly.
- The Layers panel shows the object as `Logo □□ □□ □□`.
- The document tab shows `□□□□.vectorcraft`.

**Expected result**
The UI shows the same characters as the canvas.

**Screenshot**
![Canvas renders CJK correctly; Layers panel and document tab show missing-glyph boxes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/cjk-tofu.png)

**Where it comes from**
`install_fonts()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` registers Source Sans 3 and JetBrains Mono plus egui's default fonts, none of which has CJK glyphs. The canvas text engine (`crates/text`) finds system fonts, which is why the artwork is fine and only the UI isn't. Possible fixes: add the platform's CJK system fonts (e.g. Microsoft YaHei, Yu Gothic or Malgun Gothic on Windows) as fallbacks in `install_fonts`, or bundle an OFL font such as Noto Sans CJK, which is large.

This is separate from #36, which is about the typefaces offered for type objects.

**Environment**
- VectorCraft built from `main` at 0c65fe7 (also in v0.1.1)
- Windows 11 Pro

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Window opens taller than the screen on 1600×900 and smaller displays, hiding the status bar
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
The main window always opens at 1440×900 points, whatever the size of the screen. On a 1600×900 display, which is common on laptops, it's taller than the area above the taskbar, so the hint bar and status bar (zoom level, artboard navigation, coordinates) are hidden behind the taskbar and below the bottom of the screen. On a 1366×768 display, or on a 1920×1080 laptop at 150% scaling (1280×720 points), the window is larger than the screen in both directions.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Use a display whose work area is under 1440×900 points, e.g. 1600×900 with the taskbar at the bottom.
2. Launch VectorCraft.

**Actual result**
The window is 1440×900 and starts at (26, 26). Its bottom edge is at y = 926 while the work area ends at y = 852, so the bottom 74 pt of the UI is unreachable until the window is moved, resized or maximized. This happens on every launch, because the window size isn't remembered.

**Expected result**
The first window fits inside the monitor's work area, for example by clamping the default size to it or opening maximized on small screens. Ideally the last window size and position are remembered too.

**Screenshot**
The taskbar is drawn as a plain dark bar here:

![VectorCraft window extending below the taskbar on a 1600×900 screen](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/window-overflow.png)

**Where it comes from**
`apps/vectorcraft/src/main.rs`: `ViewportBuilder::default().with_inner_size([1440.0, 900.0])`, with no check against the monitor size. The v0.1.1 release, which still had the OS title bar, overflows the same way.

**Environment**
- VectorCraft built from `main` at 0c65fe7
- Windows 11 Pro, 1600×900 at 100% scaling, taskbar at the bottom (work area 1600×852)

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Ctrl + numpad plus (and Ctrl+Shift+=) do not zoom in
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Zoom In is bound to `Ctrl+=` and only answers to that exact key. Other common ways of pressing "Ctrl and plus" do nothing:

| Keys (Windows, US layout) | Result |
|---|---|
| `Ctrl` + `=` | zooms in ✅ |
| `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `=` (Ctrl and +) | nothing ❌ |
| `Ctrl` + numpad `+` | nothing ❌ |
| `Ctrl` + numpad `-` | zooms out ✅ |
| `Ctrl` + `-` | zooms out ✅ |

From the code, the same should happen on layouts where `+` has its own key (German, Nordic, Swiss…): `Ctrl` and `+` won't zoom in there either. I tested on a US layout only.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document.
2. Press `Ctrl` + numpad `+` a few times: the zoom level stays the same.
3. Press `Ctrl` + numpad `-`: it zooms out, so numpad minus works but plus doesn't.

**Expected result**
`Ctrl` with the numpad `+`, or with `+` typed any other way, zooms in, just as both minus keys zoom out.

**Screenshot**
Zoom In and Zoom Out in the View menu:

![View menu: Zoom In Ctrl+=, Zoom Out Ctrl+-](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/view-menu-ctrl.png)

**Where it comes from**
`parse("Cmd+=")` in `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs` produces `Key::Equals`. The numpad `+`, and `+` on any layout, arrive from egui as `Key::Plus`, so the shortcut never matches. `-` works because both minus keys arrive as `Key::Minus`. A fix is coming in a PR.

**Environment**
- VectorCraft built from `main` at 0c65fe7
- Windows 11 Pro, US keyboard with a numpad

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Toolbar and panel icon strip are cut off with no way to scroll in short windows
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
When the window is shorter than about 760 pt, the bottom of the left toolbar and of the panel icon strip are cut off by the hint bar, and neither can be scrolled. title: Bug: Clicking with the Type tool leaves empty, invisible text objects in the document
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Every click with the Type tool creates a point-type object immediately. If you then type nothing (press Escape, switch tools or click somewhere else), the empty object stays in the document. It's invisible on the canvas, but it shows up as a `<Text>` row in the Layers panel, adds a "Type" step to the undo history, and is saved with the document. Clicking around with the Type tool, or clicking it by accident, litters the file with empty objects.

In Illustrator, point type that's left empty is discarded when you leave it, so nothing remains.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. New document, pick the Type tool (T).
2. Click on the artboard and, without typing anything, press Escape.
3. Click on the artboard again, then switch to the Rectangle tool.
4. Pick the Type tool again and click in two different places.
5. Open the Layers panel.

**Actual result**
The artboard is empty, but the layer contains four `<Text>` objects (zero width, no characters) and the history has four "Type" steps.

**Expected result**
Empty point type is removed when editing ends (Escape, switching tools, clicking elsewhere), so it never reaches the document or the history. Area type and type on a path made from an existing path may want to keep their frame, as Illustrator does.

**Screenshot**
![Empty artboard; Layers panel lists four empty Text objects](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/empty-point-type.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/tools/src/text.rs`: `on_up()` runs `text.create` with `"text": ""` on mouse-up, and `finish()` (used for Escape, clicking elsewhere and leaving the tool) only ends the session. It never checks whether the object it was editing is still empty. Object ▸ Path ▸ Clean Up can remove empty text afterwards (`crates/engine/src/cmd/pathops.rs`), but users shouldn't have to.

**Environment**
- VectorCraft built from `main` at 0c65fe7
- Windows 11 Pro

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Control channel / MCP: modifiers sent with ui.key and ui.click are ignored
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
`ui.key` and `ui.click` / `ui.drag` on the control channel (and so agents driving the app) accept `shift`, `alt`, `ctrl` and `cmd`, but most of the app never sees those modifiers. The modifiers are attached to the synthetic key and pointer events, while most handlers read egui's live modifier state (`i.modifiers`), which comes from the real keyboard. Agents therefore can't do anything that needs a held modifier, even though the README promises they can drive every tool gesture "the way a person does".

**Steps to reproduce** (with one object selected; JSON lines on the control port)

| Request | Expected (same as real keys/mouse) | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `{"method":"ui.key","params":{"key":"ArrowDown","shift":true}}` | nudges 10 pt | nudges 1 pt |
| `{"method":"ui.key","params":{"key":"ArrowRight","alt":true}}` | duplicates and nudges (object count +1) | only nudges 1 pt, no copy |
| `{"method":"ui.click","params":{"x":…,"y":…,"shift":true}}` on a Layers row's selection square | adds the object to the selection (`[3, 2]`) | replaces the selection (`[2]`) |

With the real keyboard and mouse on the same build, Shift+↓ moves 10 pt, Alt+→ makes a copy, and Shift-clicking the selection square gives `[3, 2]`. The app logic is fine; only control-channel input loses its modifiers.

**Where it comes from**
`VectorcraftApp::raw_input_hook` in `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` appends the queued synthetic events to `raw.events` but leaves `raw.modifiers` as it is. About 30 places in `crates/ui-egui/src` read `i.modifiers` / `ui.input(|i| i.modifiers…)`, for example the arrow nudge in `shortcuts.rs` (`let m = ctx.input(|i| i.modifiers)`), the selection square in `panels/layers.rs`, and handlers in `canvas.rs`, `toolbar.rs`, `swatches.rs` and `appearance.rs`. They all miss modifiers sent over the control channel.

A fix in one place: when `raw_input_hook` injects a synthetic `Key` or `PointerButton` event, set `raw.modifiers` for that frame to the event's modifiers. …

title: Build: rust-version says 1.90 but the dependencies need rustc 1.95
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
`Cargo.toml` declares `rust-version = "1.90"`, but the locked dependencies need rustc **1.95**. With a toolchain from 1.90 to 1.94, cargo fails on dependency versions instead of giving the clear "package requires rustc 1.95" message `rust-version` exists for.

**Steps to reproduce**
```sh
rustup toolchain install 1.90 --profile minimal
cargo +1.90 check -p vectorcraft-ui-egui
```

**Actual result**
```
  ecolor@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  egui@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  egui_extras@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  emath@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  epaint@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  epaint_default_fonts@0.36.2 requires rustc 1.95
  hayro-interpret@0.7.0 requires rustc 1.92
  hayro-syntax@0.7.2 requires rustc 1.92
  krilla@0.8.2 requires rustc 1.92
Either upgrade rustc or select compatible dependency versions with
`cargo update <name>@<current-ver> --precise <compatible-ver>`
```

**Expected result**
`rust-version` matches what the workspace really needs. Clippy on 1.95 passes for `vectorcraft-ui-egui` (with the allowance noted below), so `rust-version = "1.95"` seems right.

**Also seen**
With clippy 1.95, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` stops on `clippy::collapsible_match` at `crates/engine/src/cmd/pathops.rs:761` (`if empty_text && t.plain_text().trim().is_empty()` inside a `match` arm). Newer clippy versions don't seem to flag it, so this only affects someone running clippy on the minimum toolchain.

**Environment**
- `main` at 0c65fe7, Windows 11, rustup with x86_64-pc-windows-gnu toolchains 1.90, 1.95 and 1.99

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: WebAssembly plug-ins for VectorCraft (port PhotoCraft's plug-in API, with vector object access)
author: mindmeltde
body:
PhotoCraft already has a sandboxed WebAssembly plug-in API (photocraft#52, #67, `docs/plugins.md`: wasmi host, `plugin.*` commands, Filter › Plug-ins with generated dialogs, preference folder, works natively and in the browser). VectorCraft has the *Additional Plug-ins Folder* preference but nothing loads from it yet.

**Request**
Port the same plug-in host to VectorCraft (and ideally DesignCraft) via the shared rules, extended for vector documents. Plug-in kinds that would cover most of what Illustrator users install third-party plug-ins for:

1. **Object filters**: read the selection as paths/compound paths with fills, strokes and gradients, return modified or new objects (recolouring, halftones, path clean-up, generative patterns). Undoable like any command.
2. **Live effects**: the same function registered as an effect in the Appearance stack, re-evaluated on change, so results stay editable (non-destructive).
3. **Tools** (later): a plug-in receives pointer events on the canvas plus a guide line/rectangle and returns geometry. This is what mirror/cut-style plug-ins need.

Same sandbox rules as PhotoCraft (no WASI, fuel and memory limits, transactional edits), and every plug-in exposed as a command, so it also works over the control channel and MCP.

**Why it matters**
For many Illustrator users the plug-ins are the reason they cannot switch. A small, safe ABI lets the community fill those gaps without growing the core for every niche feature.

title: Mirror & cut tool, colour-adjustment live effects and vector halftone
author: mindmeltde
body:
Feature request. These are among the most-used third-party Illustrator plug-in features in agency work. Could they be built into VectorCraft, or would they fit better as plug-ins once the plug-in API from #121 exists?

**Tools**
- **Mirror & cut**: reflect the selection across a drawn or constrained axis, cut it at the axis and rejoin both halves into closed paths/compound paths, i.e. a symmetrical object in one step. Options: axis horizontal/vertical/free, side to keep.
- **Line cut**: split all selected art along a drawn line (incl. compound paths).
- **Rectangle cut**: crop selected art to a drawn rectangle (real geometry, not a clipping mask).

**Live effects (Effect menu / Appearance, non-destructive, on vectors, live text and embedded images)**
Brightness/Contrast, Curves, Levels, Hue/Saturation, Shift to Colour, Temperature/Tint, plus a **vector halftone** effect (dot shape, frequency, angle, mono or CMYK separations, clip to object).

title: Bug: Installed fonts (Arial, Times New Roman…) are reported missing until something triggers the system font scan
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
When a document uses a font that's installed on the system but isn't one of the bundled fonts (Arial, Times New Roman…), VectorCraft only finds it if the system font folders were scanned earlier in the session. Otherwise the font is reported missing and the text is drawn in Source Sans 3. So the same file renders differently depending on what happened before it was opened.

The scan runs only when a character needs a system fallback font (any Chinese, Japanese or Korean character, for example), or when the user picks **Show System Fonts** in the Character panel menu. Opening or placing a file never triggers it.

**Steps to reproduce**
Two SVG files with identical Latin text:

```xml
<!-- a.svg -->
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="300" height="120">
  <text x="10" y="40" font-family="Arial" font-size="28" font-weight="bold" font-style="italic">Arial Bold Italic</text>
  <text x="10" y="90" font-family="Times New Roman" font-size="28">Times New Roman</text>
</svg>
```
`b.svg` is the same plus one Chinese character drawn first: `<text x="280" y="20" font-family="Arial" font-size="10">标</text>`.

```
vectorcraft-cli info a.svg   → Arial: "missing": true,  Times New Roman: "missing": true
vectorcraft-cli info b.svg   → Arial: "missing": false, Times New Roman: "missing": false
```
The app behaves the same (checked with a build of today's `main` over the control channel, `text.fonts`):
- In a fresh session, open `a.svg`: Arial and Times New Roman are `missing: true`.
- Create any text containing a Chinese character, then open `a.svg` again: both are `missing: false`, and the file renders in real Arial and Times.

**Actual result**
`a.svg` renders in Source Sans 3. Bold italic comes out as plain italic, since Source Sans 3 has no bold italic face. `b.svg` renders correctly.

**Expected result**
Fonts installed on the system are found whenever a document asks for them, whatever was opened before.

title: Bug: SVG import ignores vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" (strokes are scaled by the transform)
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
SVG import ignores `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"`. A stroke that should keep its width in screen space is scaled by its transform like any other, and the import reports no warning, so SVGs that rely on the attribute come in with strokes that are too thick.

**Steps to reproduce**
```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="200" height="200" viewBox="0 0 200 200">
  <g transform="scale(3)">
    <path d="M10 15 H55" stroke="#e33" stroke-width="4"/>
    <path d="M10 35 H55" stroke="#3a3" stroke-width="4" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"/>
  </g>
</svg>
```
Open it in VectorCraft (or `vectorcraft-cli convert in.svg out.png`) and compare with a browser.

**Actual result**
Both lines are 12 pt thick (4 × 3), and the import gives no warning: `vectorcraft-cli run --in file.svg` shows `"warnings": []` for the open step.

**Expected result**
The green line stays 4 pt thick, as in browsers. If that can't be represented, the importer should at least warn, as it does for other approximations such as `spreadMethod`.

**Screenshot**
The red line is a normal stroke and the green one has `non-scaling-stroke`, both inside `scale(3)`:

![Chrome keeps the non-scaling stroke at 4 px; VectorCraft scales it to 12](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/non-scaling-stroke.png)

**Where it comes from**
Nothing in `crates/svg/src` handles `vector-effect`. usvg 0.48 knows the attribute name (it's in its presentation-attribute list) but doesn't carry it into the tree it returns, so the importer would have to read it from the source XML. It could then divide the stroke width by the transform's scale when it bakes the transform into the path. Non-uniform scales would need a warning, the same approximation `Scale Strokes` makes.

**Environment**
- VectorCraft v0.2.0 (the signed Windows release), also `main` at 0c65fe7; no `vector-effect` handling in `crates/svg` on today's main
- Windows 11 Pro, compared with Chrome

title: Bug: SVG and CSS export write Semibold text as bold, and Light or Medium as regular
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
SVG export (when fonts aren't embedded) and the CSS Properties panel's CSS write the wrong `font-weight` for any style that isn't Regular or Bold:
- **Semibold, Demibold and Extrabold** are written as `font-weight="bold"` (700);
- **Light, Medium, Thin and other weights below 700** get no `font-weight` at all, so they're read back as Regular (400);
- **Black and Heavy** become `bold` (700) instead of 900.

Anything that reads the SVG, VectorCraft included, then draws the text heavier or lighter than it was. The text also changes width, so the layout moves.

Two of the project's own examples show it. Export `examples/neon-drive.vectorcraft` and `examples/feature-sheet.vectorcraft` to SVG, then reopen the SVG, and their Semibold lines come back Bold. These were the only differences in my SVG round trips: 0.27% and 0.76% of pixels, all of them on those lines.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a text object in Source Sans 3 **Semibold** (or open `examples/feature-sheet.vectorcraft`, whose "Pathfinder · exact booleans" caption is Semibold).
2. Export to SVG with the default options, or run `vectorcraft-cli convert feature-sheet.vectorcraft out.svg`.
3. Look at the `<text>` element, or open the SVG in VectorCraft or a browser.

**Actual result**
`font-weight="bold"`, and the text renders Bold.

**Expected result**
`font-weight="600"` (CSS weights are numbers from 100 to 900; SVG 1.1 and SVG Tiny 1.2 accept them), and the text renders Semibold again.

**Screenshot**
The original render compared with the same document after SVG export and re-import:

**Where it comes from**
`font_props()` in `crates/svg/src/css.rs`. With `numeric_weight == false` (no embedded fonts, and always for the CSS Properties panel) it writes `bold` whenever the style name *contains* "bold", "black" or "heavy", and nothing otherw…

title: Bug: SVG import ignores paint-order="stroke" on text (works on paths)
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
SVG import honours `paint-order="stroke"` on shapes (the stroke goes under the fill), but not on `<text>`. Outlined or haloed lettering, as in map labels, subtitles and stickers, comes in with the stroke painted over the letters. A wide stroke then hides them completely.

**Steps to reproduce**
```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="300" height="80">
  <path d="M10 10 h60 v30 h-60z" fill="#fc0" stroke="#000" stroke-width="10" paint-order="stroke"/>
  <text x="100" y="45" font-size="36" font-weight="bold" fill="#fc0" stroke="#000" stroke-width="8"
        paint-order="stroke">Ab</text>
</svg>
```
Open it in VectorCraft, or run `vectorcraft-cli convert in.svg out.png`, and compare with a browser.

**Actual result**
The rectangle is right: yellow fill with the black stroke outside it. The text is drawn stroke-on-top, so "Ab" becomes a black blob. The import gives no warning (`vectorcraft-cli run --in` shows `"warnings": []`).

**Expected result**
The text's stroke goes under its fill, as on the rectangle. If that can't be represented, the importer should at least warn.

**Screenshot**
![paint-order=stroke: right on the path, ignored on the text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/paint-order-text.png)

(The letter shapes differ only because the browser's default font is a serif; the stroke order is the bug.)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/svg/src/import.rs` maps `usvg::PaintOrder::StrokeAndFill` to `[stroke, fill]` in `appearance()`, which only paths use. The text import in `crates/svg/src/import/text.rs` never reads the paint order. Since type can carry an object-level appearance with a Characters row, `paint-order="stroke"` on text could become an object appearance whose stroke sits under Characters. Failing that, it could warn like the other approximations. SVG export writes `paint-order` only for paths, so VectorCraft's own SVGs aren't affected. This is about SVGs from elsewhere.

title: Bug: Undo while typing (or mid-drag) also undoes the step before, and the typing cannot be redone
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Pressing Undo while something is still in progress, such as typing with the Type tool or dragging an object, throws that work away **and also undoes the step before it**. What was being typed can't be redone, so it's lost.

**Steps to reproduce (typing)**
1. With the Type tool, click the artboard and type `abc`.
2. Press ← then → (moving the caret ends that typing step), and type `def`.
3. Press Ctrl+Z once.
4. Press Ctrl+Shift+Z twice.

**Actual result**
- Step 3: the text is **empty**. Both `def` and `abc` are gone.
- Step 4: only `abc` comes back. `def` is lost; nothing can redo it.

**Expected result**
- Step 3 undoes only the typing in progress, leaving `abc`.
- Redo brings `def` back.

**Steps to reproduce (dragging)**
Draw a rectangle, start dragging it with the Selection tool, and press Ctrl+Z before releasing. The drag is cancelled, **and the rectangle is deleted**, because its creation is undone too.

**Screenshot**
![Typing abcdef, one Ctrl+Z removes both steps, redo only restores abc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/undo-while-typing.png)

(The caret also stays where the longer text ended, as panels 2 and 3 show.)

**Where it comes from**
`undo()` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/edit.rs` starts with `s.cancel_interaction()?`, which rolls back the open interaction (the typing session or drag preview) without recording it. It then pops the previous history entry. One Undo therefore removes two steps, and the first never reaches the redo stack.

Committing the interaction instead (`s.commit_interaction()?`) makes the in-progress work the step that Undo takes back, so Redo can restore it. `commit_interaction` is a no-op when nothing is open or nothing changed. A PR follows.

**Environment**
- Reproduced on a release build of `main` at 8adc629 (Windows 11), driven through the control channel. `undo()` is unchanged on `main` at cccdf96, and the v0.2.0 release has the same code.

title: Bug: Renaming a layer in the Layers panel never takes effect (Enter does not commit)
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Renaming a layer or object in the Layers panel never takes effect. Double-clicking a row's name opens the name field, and you can type in it, but Enter doesn't commit the new name, and neither does clicking elsewhere or pressing Escape. The field stays open, and the layer keeps its old name.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open the Layers panel and double-click "Layer 1".
2. Select all, type `Sky`, press Enter.
3. Click the canvas.

**Actual result**
The field stays open showing `Sky` after step 2 and after step 3. The layer is still named "Layer 1" (`document.inspect` and every other view say so).

**Expected result**
Enter, or a click elsewhere, renames the layer to `Sky` and closes the field; Escape closes it without renaming.

**Screenshot**
![The rename field stays open after Enter and after a click on the canvas](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/layer-rename.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/layers.rs`: the name field calls `te.request_focus()` every frame, just before checking `te.lost_focus()`. When Enter (or Escape, or a click elsewhere) makes the single-line field give up focus, the request takes it straight back, so `lost_focus()` is never true and the rename is never committed. The Artboards panel's rename already does it the working way: `if !te.has_focus() && !te.lost_focus() { te.request_focus(); }`. No test covered renaming a layer. A PR follows.

**Environment**
- `main` at 8adc629, release build on Windows 11, driven through the control channel. The code is the same on today's `main` (1c46c4c).

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Shift+drag on a selected object deselects it instead of moving it constrained
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
With the Selection tool, holding Shift and dragging an object that is already selected doesn't move it. As soon as the button goes down, the object leaves the selection, and the drag does nothing. Nothing is added to History.

The same Shift+drag works on an object that isn't selected: it selects the object and moves it, constrained to 45° steps. Pressing Shift only after the drag has started also works. In Illustrator, a Shift+drag on a selected object moves the selection with the constraint. Only a Shift+click without dragging takes it out of the selection.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Draw a rectangle and click it with the Selection tool, so that it is selected.
2. Hold Shift, press inside the rectangle (away from the bounding-box handles) and drag to the right.

**Actual result**
The rectangle is deselected as soon as the button goes down, and it stays where it was.

**Expected result**
The rectangle moves horizontally, constrained by Shift, and stays selected.

**Screenshot**
![Top: the rectangle selected. Bottom: after holding Shift, pressing inside it and dragging right, it is deselected and hasn't moved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/shift-drag.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/tools/src/select.rs`, on pointer down over an object with Shift held:
```rust
out.push(Action::Exec("select.toggle".into(), json!({ "id": top.0 })));
if cx.selection.contains(top) {
    self.state = State::Idle;
    return out;
}
```
For an object that is already selected, it toggles it off right away and goes idle, so no move can start. Deferring that toggle to the release, and dropping it once a drag begins, fixes it. A PR follows.

**Environment**
- `main` at 856e36c, release build on Windows 11, driven with real mouse and keyboard input.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: A click just outside the canvas edge acts as a click in the centre of the view
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
A click a few pixels *outside* the canvas is handled as a click in the **centre of the view**. It can land just below the document tabs, at the canvas's right edge next to the panel strip, or just above the hint bar. With the Selection tool it selects whatever is in the middle of the view. With the Type tool it starts text there, and drawing tools draw from there. The pointer can be anywhere along the edge; the click always lands in the centre.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document and choose the Type tool.
2. Click at the far right of the thin gap between the document tab bar and the canvas: about 2 px above the canvas, away from any tab.
3. Type `Oops`.

**Actual result**
The text is created in the middle of the view, far from where you clicked. Likewise with the Selection tool: with an object in the middle of the view, the same click selects it, whatever was selected before.

**Expected result**
A click outside the canvas doesn't reach the tools.

**Screenshot**
![Type tool: a click just below the tab bar, at the top right, starts the text "Oops" at the centre of the view](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/canvas-edge-click.png)

**Where it comes from**
`handle_input` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`:
```rust
let hover = pointer.hover_pos().filter(|p| rect.contains(*p));
// …
if pointer.primary_pressed() && resp.hovered() && !middle_pan {
    // …
    let p = hover.unwrap_or(rect.center());
```
egui reports the canvas response as hovered for a pointer a few pixels outside its rect (its interaction radius), but `hover` only counts points inside the rect. For a press in that band, `p` falls back to `rect.center()`. The middle-button pan has the same fallback. A PR follows that only starts a press when the pointer is on the canvas.

**Environment**
- `main` at aafd565, release build on Windows 11. Found with real mouse input; the control channel's `ui.click` reproduces it too.

_Found while testing Vect…

title: Bug: Illustrator EPS files can't be opened: five PostScript gaps in the AGM/CoolType prolog, and the TIFF preview fallback fails too
author: EthanSuquet
body:
**Version:** vectorcraft-cli 0.3.1, main @ 571881a · macOS 26 (Darwin 25.6), Apple M2 Max, release build

### What happens

EPS files saved by Adobe Illustrator (CS-era and later, with the `Adobe_AGM_Core` / `Adobe_CoolType_Core`
procsets in the prolog and a DOS binary header with a TIFF preview) fail to open:

```
vectorcraft-cli convert logo.eps out.svg
can't open `logo.eps`: this PostScript file can't be read (a PostScript error (undefinedresource in `Generic`)): save it as PDF or SVG in the app that made it
```

Patching each error in turn shows a chain of five interpreter gaps; each one reproduces on its own with
the tiny files below (all fail on 571881a). A file then also misses the preview fallback (last section).

### Repros (each a complete EPS)

Header for all: `%!PS-Adobe-3.0 EPSF-3.0` / `%%BoundingBox: 0 0 100 100` / `%%EndComments`, then the line
below, then `0 0 1 setrgbcolor 10 10 80 80 rectfill showpage`.

| # | Line | Actual on main | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `/Generic /Category findresource pop` | `undefinedresource in Generic` | the predefined `Generic` category (PLRM 3.9.2). Illustrator's prolog runs `[/CSA /Gradient /Procedure] { /Generic /Category findresource dup length dict copy /Category defineresource pop } forall` |
| 2 | `clipsave 0 0 50 50 rectclip cliprestore` | `it uses clipsave, which VectorCraft's PostScript reader doesn't know` | LL3 `clipsave`/`cliprestore` |
| 3 | `/Level2? systemdict /languagelevel known dup { pop systemdict /languagelevel get 2 ge } if def` | `typecheck in ge` (the `get` returns the operator) | `3` — Adobe interpreters and Ghostscript store `languagelevel` in systemdict as an integer; CoolType's prolog relies on it |
| 4 | `/a 4 array def 1 2 a 0 2 getinterval astore pop a 0 get 1 eq { 0 0 1 setrgbcolor } { 1 0 0 setrgbcolor } ifelse` (and no fixed colour line) | red square: `getinterval` returned a copy, so `astore` didn't reach `a` | blue: a subarray shares storage with its array (PLRM `getinterval`)…

title: Bug: Some panel flyouts (Separations Preview, Align…) extend over the panel icon column
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Several panels that open as a flyout beside the panel icon column extend over that column, covering part of its icons. Separations Preview is the clearest case (View → Proof Setup → Customize… or Window → Separations Preview): it covers the left half of the icons next to it. In other panels the overlap is smaller and mostly hides the column's border.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document, select an object, and open Window → Separations Preview.
2. Look at the panel icon column to the right of the flyout.

**Actual result**
The flyout runs over the icon column. Measured in a headless frame, the flyouts that overrun the column's left edge are:
- Align by 24 pt;
- Separations Preview and Transform by 18 pt;
- Stroke and Attributes by 16 pt;
- Gradient by 14 pt.

**Expected result**
Every flyout keeps the 6 pt gap the narrower panels keep, and the icons stay fully visible.

**Screenshot**
![Top: main, the Separations Preview flyout covers the panel icons. Bottom: with the fix, it keeps the same gap as the other panels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/flyout-over-icons.png)

**Where it comes from**
`floating_panel` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dock.rs` places the flyout `Area` by its left edge (`fixed_pos(x, 110)`, with `x` 262 pt left of the column) and sets its width to 256. Content wider than that, such as Separations Preview's profile dropdowns (a fixed 210 pt next to the "CMYK:" and "Assign:" labels), makes the frame grow, and since the left edge is fixed it grows to the right, over the column. A PR follows that pins the flyout by its right edge instead, so a wider panel grows towards the canvas.

**Environment**
- `main` at aafd565, release build on Windows 11, at 1600 × 852.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Dialogs without a maximum width (Clean Up, Blend Options…) stretch across the whole window
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Many dialogs stretch across the **entire window width** however little they contain. Examples:
- Object → Path → Clean Up…, with three check boxes;
- Object → Blend → Blend Options…, with two rows;
- Type → Smart Punctuation… and every other dialog built from the generic parameter form;
- most dialogs that don't set a maximum width.

In a 1600-point window, the Clean Up dialog is 1586 points wide, with its fields at the far left and OK/Cancel at the far right.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document, select an object, and choose Object → Path → Clean Up… or Object → Blend → Blend Options….

**Actual result**
The dialog spans the whole window (see the "main" rows below).

**Expected result**
A compact dialog sized to its fields and centred, like Document Setup or the Color Picker (which set a maximum width).

**Screenshot**
![Clean Up and Blend Options: on main each dialog spans the whole window; with the fix each is sized to its fields](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/dialog-width.png)

**Where it comes from**
`show` in `crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/mod.rs` lays out the OK/Cancel row right to left with the width `ui.available_width()`. A dialog without a `max_width` has the whole window as its maximum width, so the row, and with it the window, takes all of it. The code already guards against the same thing for height ("The button row is as tall as the buttons…"). A PR follows that makes the row as wide as the fields above it.

**Environment**
- `main` at b05e575, release build on Windows 11, at 1600 × 852.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Type tool: dragging across text that isn't being edited only places the caret, it doesn't select
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
With the Type tool, pressing on a text object that isn't being edited and dragging across some of its characters doesn't select them. It only places the caret where the press was. Typing then inserts at that point instead of replacing the dragged-over text. Only a second drag, once the text is being edited, selects. In Illustrator, and text editors generally, one press-and-drag over existing text selects it.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Create a point text object `Alpha Beta Gamma` and deselect it.
2. With the Type tool, press just before `Beta`, drag to just after it, release.
3. Type `X`.

**Actual result**
After step 2 there is only a caret before `Beta`, with no selection. Step 3 gives `Alpha XBeta Gamma`.

**Expected result**
Step 2 selects `Beta`, and step 3 gives `Alpha X Gamma`.

**Screenshot**
![After dragging across "Beta" with the Type tool, only a caret is placed before it and nothing is selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/type-first-drag.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/tools/src/text.rs`: on `PointerKind::Down`, only a press inside the text *being edited* (`hit_edited`) starts a selection (`selecting = true`). A press elsewhere is kept as a possible drag to create area type (`press`/`drag`). On release, `on_up` sees the press was on existing text and starts editing with the caret at the press point, ignoring the drag. A PR follows that starts editing at the press when it lands on text, so the same drag selects.

**Environment**
- `main` at e960baa, release build on Windows 11, with real mouse input.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Guides can't be dragged out of the rulers
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Guides can't be dragged out of the rulers. With rulers shown (View → Rulers → Show Rulers, Ctrl+R), pressing in the top or left ruler and dragging into the canvas does nothing: no guide preview, no guide on release, no History entry. Dragging from a ruler is the usual way to make a guide in Illustrator: the top ruler gives a horizontal guide, the left ruler a vertical one. Today guides can only come from View → Guides → Make Guides, which converts paths, or from the `guide.add` command.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document and show the rulers (Ctrl+R).
2. Press in the top ruler, drag down onto the artboard and release.

**Actual result**
Nothing happens. The document's `guides` stay empty, and the release just lands on whatever is under the pointer.

**Expected result**
A horizontal guide where the button was released, previewed while dragging. Likewise a vertical guide from the left ruler.

**Screenshot**
![Rulers shown; a drag from the top ruler down to the artboard leaves no guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/ruler-guide.png)

**Where it comes from**
`rulers()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` only paints the rulers: it allocates no interaction for them. Nothing in the UI calls `guide.add`. The engine side exists (`guide.add {vertical, pos}` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/docmenu.rs`), so a drag on the ruler rects could preview a line and call it on release inside the canvas. ROADMAP's "Guides, grids, smart guides, snapping, rulers" row doesn't list this as missing.

**Environment**
- `main` at e960baa, release build on Windows 11, with real mouse input.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: An area-type frame dragged with the Type tool lands 12 pt below the dragged rectangle
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Dragging with the Type tool to create area type draws the marquee where the mouse goes. On release, the frame is created 12 pt lower than that marquee. Its width and height match the drag, but the whole frame moves down by 12 pt, so its bottom edge no longer meets the cursor. The offset is in document points, so it's the same at every zoom level: 12 px at 100%, 48 px at 400%. Vertical Type does the same.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. New document. Zoom to 400% so the offset is easy to see.
2. Choose the Type tool (T).
3. Drag from (40, 40) pt to (180, 110) pt, and watch the dashed marquee.
4. Release, then check the frame or the Properties panel.

**Actual result**
The frame is at x 40, y 52, w 140, h 70, which is 12 pt below where it was dragged. Properties shows Y 87.125 pt (centre) instead of 75 pt.

**Expected result**
The frame is the dragged rectangle: x 40, y 40, w 140, h 70. That's what the marquee showed and what Illustrator creates.

**Screenshot**
![Top: the Type tool's marquee during a real mouse drag. Bottom: after release, the blue area-type frame sits 12 pt below the red rectangle that was dragged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/area-type-offset.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/tools/src/text.rs`, `on_up`: a drag becomes `text.create` with `"y": r.y0 + 12.0`. `text.create` makes the area frame `Rect::new(0, 0, w, h)` at `(x, y)` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/create.rs`), so the frame's top-left is `(x, y)`. The extra 12 pt pushes the frame down. The layout already puts the first line inside the frame, so no baseline offset is needed. A PR follows that passes `r.y0`.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` at e960baa on Windows 11, with real mouse input. The line is unchanged at 83faf56.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Area type can't be resized with the mouse: handles stretch the glyphs, Direct Selection moves the whole object
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
There's no way to resize an area-type frame with the mouse.
- **Selection tool:** dragging one of its bounding-box handles scales the glyphs. They stretch, unevenly unless Shift is held, and the text doesn't reflow, so overflow text stays hidden. History records the drag as "Scale".
- **Direct Selection tool:** the frame's corners can't be picked. Dragging one moves the whole object ("Move").

In Illustrator, both drags resize or reshape the type area, and the text reflows at its own size. Adobe's help ("Resize a type area") lists dragging a bounding-box handle with the Selection tool and dragging the frame's edge or corner with the Direct Selection tool. That's how you make room for overflow text. Here the only option is to make the type again. Area Type Options has no width or height either.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make area type with overflow, e.g. with the Type tool drag a 120 × 40 pt frame and type three sentences. The same works through the control channel with `text.create` `{"x":40,"y":40,"size":12,"area":{"width":120,"height":40},"text":"…"}`.
2. With the Selection tool, drag the bottom-right handle to make the box 160 × 100 pt.
3. Undo. With the Direct Selection tool, drag the frame's bottom-right corner.

**Actual result**
- Step 2: the 12 pt type is drawn 1.33× wider and 2.5× taller. The same two lines show and the rest is still hidden. The Character panel still says 12 pt.
- Step 3: the whole text object moves. The frame keeps its shape.

**Expected result**
- Step 2: the frame becomes 160 × 100 pt and the 12 pt text reflows into it, with more lines visible.
- Step 3: the corner moves, which reshapes the frame, and the text reflows.

**Screenshot**
![1: overflowing area type selected. 2: after dragging its corner handle the glyphs are stretched and the same two lines show. 3: dragging the frame corner with Direct Selection moved the whole object](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/area-type-res…

title: Bug: inspect_document reports fill and stroke "None" for type whose characters are painted
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

`inspect_document` (engine `document.inspect`) reports a plain Type node's `fill` and `stroke` as `"None"` and its `strokeWidth` as `0`, even when its characters carry a fill and a stroke. That holds whether the paint comes from `add_text`'s `color` or from `set_paint` / `paint.setFill` on the type object. `text.getRange` and SVG export show the paint, and `paint.proxies` shows the fill. The same node's `strokeOptions` already comes from the first run's character stroke, so one node summary mixes two sources. An MCP client that reads paint back through `inspect_document`, the tool documented for it, concludes that coloured text is unpainted and cannot confirm a paint change it just made.

title: Bug: `docs/mcp.md`, the `export` tool description and CLI usage omit formats that `document.formats` reads and writes (DXF, EPS, EMF, WMF, SVGZ, templates)
author: coygeek
body:

## Summary

MCP clients see the `save_file` tool described as "Save the active document in the native .vectorcraft format." title: Bug: `docs/mcp.md` says `document.inspect` shows swatch-linked paint as `{type, color, swatch, tint}`, but it reports a label string
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

The "Tints of global and spot colours" section of `docs/mcp.md` says that `paint.proxies` and `document.inspect` both show a fill or stroke linked to a global or spot swatch as `{type: "solid", color, swatch, tint}` (`tint` left out at 100 %). `paint.proxies` does. `document.inspect`, and with it the MCP `inspect_document` tool, reports the same paint as a display label such as `"G1 40% (#ff9999)"` or `"G1 (#ff0000)"` on the object's node, and in the same form in the reply's `paint` summary of the current paint. An MCP client that follows the docs and reads `swatch` and `tint` from `inspect_document` finds a string instead of the documented object.

## Runtime or environment

- Source: `main` at commit `116ff3eee7703321cf68d0c8b9218890434feefc` (checked 2026-10-06). The same sentence is on `v0.3.1` (line 661).
- Runtime: the published `v0.3.1` release, `vectorcraft-cli-0.3.1-macos-universal.zip` (sha256 matches `SHA256SUMS.txt`), on macOS 27.0.1 arm64, running `vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless` and `vectorcraft-cli run`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start `vectorcraft-cli mcp --headless` and send `initialize`, then `notifications/initialized`.

title: Vertical text: "月" overlaps the digits "22" in "10月22日まで"
author: htdtkshi
body:
## Summary
With `text.create ... "vertical": true`, the string `はただ商店 秋のセール 10月22日まで` renders with the glyph "月" drawn on top of the digits "22" in the exported PNG.

## Environment
- Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu, headless), vectorcraft 0.3.1, `vectorcraft-cli mcp` (25 tools), font `Noto Sans CJK JP` (fonts-noto-cjk)

## Steps to reproduce
Via MCP/command API, in a new document:
1. `text.create {"x":520,"y":100,"text":"はただ商店 秋のセール 10月22日まで","vertical":true,"size":28,"font":"Noto Sans CJK JP"}`
2. Export to PNG (`file.export`), or `vectorcraft-cli convert` the saved .vectorcraft to PNG.


## Expected
Each character occupies its own cell in the column; digits are spaced so that neighbouring glyphs do not overlap.

## Actual
The digits "10" and "22" are laid out sideways-offset from the column, and "月" overlaps "22". The README notes vertical text support is initial, so this may be a known limitation.

## Notes
- n=2 (byte-identical PNG, md5 462ae00c...).
- Duplicate check (storytold/vectorcraft, --state all): "vertical", "vertical text", "writing mode", "tategaki", "overlap", "Japanese", "CJK", "kerning" -> none on this behavior (#250 is about the Type tool drag rectangle, #81 closed is UI glyph boxes).

title: Bug: Double-clicking the Hand, Zoom, Rotate, Scale, Reflect or Shear tool does nothing
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Double-clicking these tool buttons in the toolbar does nothing except select the tool:
- **Hand tool:** should fit the artboard in the window, like View › Fit Artboard in Window.
- **Zoom tool:** should show the document at 100%, like View › Actual Size.
- **Rotate, Scale, Reflect and Shear tools:** should open the Rotate, Scale, Reflect and Shear dialogs for the selection, like Object › Transform.

In Illustrator these are standard double-clicks, and Adobe's help documents each one. VectorCraft already has the commands and dialogs.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document and zoom to something other than 100%, e.g. 333%.
2. Double-click the Hand tool in the toolbar.
3. Double-click the Zoom tool.
4. Select an object and double-click the Rotate tool. Repeat with Scale, Reflect and Shear.

**Actual result**
Each tool becomes the active tool. The view doesn't change (it stays at 333%), and no dialog opens.

**Expected result**
- Step 2 fits the artboard in the window.
- Step 3 shows 100%.
- Step 4 opens the Rotate dialog (then Scale, Reflect, Shear) to transform the selection about its centre.

No screenshot, since nothing visible happens.

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/toolbar.rs`: a double-click on a tool button runs `tool.options {tool}`. `open_options` only handles `gradient`, `eyedropper`, `blend`, `perspectiveGrid`, `printTiling` and the Liquify tools. Every other tool gets "the … tool has no options", which the toolbar drops. The existing test even uses `zoom` as its example of a tool with no options. A PR follows that maps:
- `hand` → `view.fitArtboard`;
- `zoom` → `view.actualSize`;
- `rotate`, `scale`, `reflect`, `shear` → the dialogs Object › Transform opens (`menus::invoke("object.rotate")`, …), when something is selected.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` at e960baa on Windows 11, with real mouse double-clicks. `open_options` is unchanged at 7ce27ca.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Free Transform's Free Distort, Perspective Distort and Shear can't be reached with the mouse
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
With the mouse, the Free Transform tool (E) can only scale, rotate and move. Its Free Distort, Perspective Distort and Shear can't be reached.

The tool's docs (`crates/tools/src/xform/free.rs`) give the classic gestures:
- Free Distort: Ctrl (Cmd) while dragging a corner;
- Perspective Distort: Ctrl+Alt+Shift while dragging a corner;
- Shear: Ctrl while dragging a side handle.

Neither order of keys works with real input:
- **Ctrl pressed after the drag starts.** This is how Adobe documents it: "start dragging a corner handle, then hold down Ctrl". The tool decides what the drag does on the press and never looks at the keys again, so the drag stays a scale.
- **Ctrl held before pressing.** The canvas turns any Ctrl+press into the temporary Selection tool (`handle_input` in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`), so the Free Transform tool never sees the press. The temporary Selection tool scales instead.

There's no other way in, either. The tool's `mode` option (`perspective` / `distort`) works through `tool.setOption`, but nothing in the UI sets it. Illustrator has its Free Transform widget for that; here the Control bar only has options for Mirror & Cut and Puppet Warp.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Draw a rectangle and keep it selected. Press E.
2. Start dragging the bottom-right corner handle, then hold Ctrl and keep dragging. Release.
3. Undo. Hold Ctrl, press on the same corner, drag, release.
4. Undo. Do step 2 again with Ctrl+Alt+Shift, then with Ctrl on a side handle.

**Actual result**
Every variant is a plain scale, recorded in History as "Scale". The box stays a rectangle while dragging.

**Expected result**
- Ctrl on a corner moves just that corner (Free Distort, "Distort" in History).
- Ctrl+Alt+Shift moves the corners symmetrically (Perspective Distort).
- Ctrl on a side handle shears.

title: Bug: Ctrl with another tool always switches to the Selection tool, not the last-used selection tool
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Holding Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) with a non-selection tool active, such as the Pen, switches temporarily to the Selection tool for the drag. It's always the Selection tool. In Illustrator, Ctrl switches to the *last-used* selection tool: Selection, Direct Selection or Group Selection. Adobe's default keyboard shortcuts list it under "Keys for selecting" as "Switch to last-used selection tool".

This matters most while drawing with the Pen. You use Direct Selection (A), take the Pen (P), and Ctrl-drag an anchor to adjust it. In VectorCraft, that same Ctrl-drag picks up the whole path with the Selection tool and moves it.

2. Choose the Direct Selection tool and click the triangle's edge.
3. Press P for the Pen tool.
4. Hold Ctrl, press on the anchor at (200, 120) and drag it to (240, 100). Release.

**Actual result**
While Ctrl is held, the toolbar and status bar show the Selection tool. The whole triangle moves by (40, −20), recorded as "Move" in History. Afterwards the Pen tool is back.

**Expected result**
With Direct Selection used last, Ctrl gives the Direct Selection tool. The drag moves just that anchor, and the Pen comes back afterwards. With Group Selection used last, Ctrl gives Group Selection, and with Selection used last, Selection.

Nothing remembers which selection tool was used last. A PR follows that records it in `UiState` whenever one of …

title: Bug: Ctrl+Space doesn't zoom in (and Ctrl+Alt+Space doesn't zoom out); Space always pans
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Holding Ctrl+Space (Cmd+Space on macOS) doesn't give the Zoom tool for the moment, and Ctrl+Alt+Space doesn't zoom out. Any Space-held click or drag pans instead, so a Ctrl+Space click does nothing.

In Illustrator these are the standard temporary zoom keys, next to Space for the Hand tool. Adobe's default keyboard shortcuts list them under "Keys for viewing artwork":
- Ctrl+Space with a click or drag zooms in (a drag marquee-zooms);
- Ctrl+Alt+Space zooms out.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document at 250% with any tool, e.g. Selection.
2. Hold Ctrl+Space and click on the canvas. Release the keys.
3. Hold Ctrl+Alt+Space and click.

**Actual result**
The zoom stays at 250% both times. The cursor shows the open hand while the keys are down.

**Expected result**
- Step 2 zooms in one step (300%) around the click.
- Step 3 zooms out one step.
- While the keys are down, the cursor is the zoom-in or zoom-out magnifier.
- A Ctrl+Space drag zooms to the dragged box, like the Zoom tool.

No screenshot, since nothing visible happens.

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `handle_input`: `pan_mode = space || tool == "hand"`, checked before anything else, so Space wins whatever else is held. The cursor code does the same. The Zoom tool's click and marquee (`Drag::ZoomBox`, Alt to zoom out) already live in the canvas. A PR follows that makes held Space mean the Hand tool and Cmd+Space the Zoom tool, whatever the active tool, cursor included.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` at eac383d on Windows 11, with the real keyboard and mouse.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Shortcuts with Shift + punctuation don't fire (Bring to Front, Send to Back, Search Commands, Curvature tool)
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
On a real keyboard, the default shortcuts that combine Shift with a punctuation key don't fire. Three are command shortcuts and one is a tool shortcut:

| Shortcut | Command / tool | Result with real keys |
|---|---|---|
| Ctrl+Shift+] | Object › Arrange › Bring to Front | nothing |
| Ctrl+Shift+[ | Object › Arrange › Send to Back | nothing |
| Ctrl+Shift+/ | Help › Search Commands… (the hint bar says to press it) | nothing |
| Shift+~ | Curvature Tool | nothing |

Their unshifted neighbours work, e.g. Ctrl+] (Bring Forward) and Ctrl+[ (Send Backward), and so does Ctrl+Shift+' (Snap to Grid). The menu items work.

**Steps to reproduce**
Windows 11, US keyboard layout:
1. Draw two overlapping shapes and select the one at the back.
2. Press Ctrl+Shift+] (Bring to Front).
3. Press Ctrl+Shift+/ (Search Commands).
4. Press Shift+` (the `~` key, Curvature Tool).

**Actual result**
Nothing happens. The order doesn't change and History gets no step. The command palette doesn't open, and the tool stays the same.

**Expected result**
Bring to Front, the Search Commands palette, and the Curvature tool, as the menus and tool tips list.

No screenshot, since nothing visible happens.

**Where it comes from**
egui reports the character a key types, so with Shift held:
- `[` arrives as `Key::OpenCurlyBracket`, `]` as `CloseCurlyBracket` and `/` as `Questionmark`;
- `` ` `` arrives as the text `~`.

In `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`:
- `consume` matches the parsed chord (`Cmd+Shift+OpenBracket`…) exactly. It already makes the same allowance for `+` arriving for Shift+`=` (#83), but for nothing else.
- The single-key tool shortcuts look up the typed text (`~`), which doesn't normalize to the catalog's `Shift+~`.

A PR follows that accepts the shifted characters for these chords and looks up `Shift+<typed text>` for tool and single-key command shortcuts.

title: Bug: Double-clicking type with the Selection tool doesn't place a caret; typing then triggers shortcuts (X swaps fill/stroke)
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Double-clicking type with the Selection tool switches to the Type tool, but nothing is being edited and there's no caret. Typing right after doesn't go into the text. Each key is taken as a tool or command shortcut instead. Typing X, for example, swaps the selected text's fill and stroke, so black type becomes outlined type, and History records it.

In Illustrator, double-clicking type with the Selection tool switches to the Type tool and puts the insertion point where you clicked, so you can type straight away. Adobe's help: "double-click the text with the Selection tool".

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Point type "Hello world", 24 pt, black. Deselect it.
2. With the Selection tool, double-click in the middle of the text.
3. Type X.

**Actual result**
After step 2 the Type tool is active, but `toolOptions.editing` is null and there's no caret. After step 3 the text is still "Hello world", and its fill and stroke are swapped (fill None, stroke black).

**Expected result**
After step 2 the caret is at the click, between the characters there. Step 3 inserts X at that point, and the fill and stroke stay as they were.

**Screenshot**
![After double-clicking the text with the Selection tool and typing X: the text is unchanged but drawn as outlines, because X swapped its fill and stroke](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/double-click-type.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/tools/src/select.rs`: a `DoubleClick` on text returns only `Action::SwitchTool("type")`, so the Type tool starts idle. The Type tool already places the caret when it gets a click on existing type (`edit_at`), but after the switch it never gets one. A PR follows in which the canvas (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`) passes the double-click's position on to the Type tool as a click after such a switch.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` at eac383d on Windows 11, with a real mouse double-click and real typing.

title: Bug: The Symbols panel takes no drag and drop: art dropped on it makes no symbol, symbols can't be dragged onto the canvas
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
The Symbols panel takes no drag and drop in either direction:
- **Art onto the panel:** dragging selected art from the canvas and releasing it over the Symbols panel does nothing. No symbol is made, and the art stays where it was.
- **A symbol onto the canvas:** a symbol in the panel can't be dragged out to place an instance where it's dropped. The only ways to place one are a double-click or the Place Symbol Instance button, which put it at the artboard's centre.

Both are standard in Illustrator. Adobe's help on creating symbols says to select the art and either click New Symbol or drag the artwork to the Symbols panel. For placing, it says to drag the symbol to the artboard. In VectorCraft the canvas already turns a Selection-tool drag off the canvas into a panel drag of the art (`PanelDrag::Art`). The Graphic Styles and Asset Export panels accept it, but the Symbols panel ignores it.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Draw a rectangle and select it with the Selection tool. Open Window › Symbols.
2. Drag the rectangle onto the Symbols panel and release.
3. Make a symbol with the panel's New Symbol button, then try to drag its thumbnail onto the artboard.

**Actual result**
- Step 2: no symbol is made (`symbol.list` stays empty), and the rectangle is unchanged.
- Step 3: the thumbnail doesn't drag.

**Expected result**
- Step 2 makes a symbol from the dragged art, as New Symbol does (`symbol.new`).
- Step 3 places an instance centred where it's dropped (`symbol.place {name, x, y}`).

title: Menu bar: hovering another top-level title does not switch open menus
author: theDavidCoen
body:
## Summary

On the in-window menu bar (Linux), opening one top-level menu (e.g. File) and then moving the pointer over Edit / Object / … does **not** open those menus. Each title needs its own click.

PhotoCraft already implements native-style behaviour via `switch_on_hover` in `menus.rs` (“while one top-level menu is open, hovering another top-level title opens that menu instead”). VectorCraft’s `menu_bar` only calls `ui.menu_button` in a loop and has no equivalent.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run VectorCraft 0.3.1 on Linux/Wayland.
2. Click **File** to open its dropdown.
3. Move the pointer sideways over **Edit**, **Object**, etc. without clicking.

## Expected

The open menu switches to the title under the pointer (Windows / macOS / PhotoCraft behaviour).

## Actual

The original menu stays open; other titles require a separate click.

## Environment

- VectorCraft 0.3.1 (linux-x86_64 AppImage)
- Linux CachyOS, Wayland

## Suggested fix

Port PhotoCraft’s `switch_on_hover` (track top-level `Response`s, `Popup::is_id_open` / `Popup::open_id`) into VectorCraft’s `menu_bar`.

title: Bug: macOS "Open With" / double-click fails: "VectorCraft cannot open files in the PDF document format"
author: benshen94
body:
## What happens

On macOS (v0.3.1, release DMG), opening a file through Finder fails with:

> The document "Fig1.pdf" could not be opened. VectorCraft cannot open files in the "PDF document" format.

This happens with right-click › Open With › VectorCraft, double-click (when VectorCraft is the chosen app), and dropping a file on the Dock icon. The same PDF opens fine with File › Open, by dragging it into the window, or with `vectorcraft-cli convert`.

## Cause

Two separate gaps:

1. **`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in` has no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`.** It only exports the `.vectorcraft` UTI, so Launch Services treats the app as unable to open any file and shows the error above before the app is involved. (The dev bundle from `cargo xtask bundle` does declare document types in `xtask/src/bundle.rs`, so this only shows up in release builds.)
2. **The app doesn't handle macOS open-document events.** Finder delivers files as `application:openURLs:` to the NSApplication delegate. winit 0.30's delegate doesn't implement it, and `main.rs` only reads files from argv. So fixing the plist alone would let the file through, but nothing would open it.

## Suggested fix (tested locally on macOS, Apple silicon)

- **Info.plist.in:** add `CFBundleDocumentTypes`: the VectorCraft UTI as `Owner`, and the other `fileio::OPEN_EXTS` extensions as `Editor` with `LSHandlerRank = Alternate`, so VectorCraft doesn't take over PDF/PNG defaults from Preview.
- **New `apps/vectorcraft/src/open_documents.rs` (macOS only):** before `run_native`, observe `NSApplicationWillFinishLaunchingNotification`. In that callback, add `application:openURLs:` to winit's delegate class with `class_addMethod`. AppKit delivers launch-time files after that notification, so both cold launch and an already-running app are covered. The handler queues the paths and wakes egui, and `App::logic` opens them with `io::open_path`, the same path that drag-and-drop uses.
  - This needs `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` scoped to that on…

title: Bug: Swatches and Brushes panels take no drag and drop: art dropped on them makes nothing, brushes can't be dragged onto paths

title: Bug: Alt-clicking a layer's eye or lock toggles only that layer, not the others
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
In the Layers panel, Alt-clicking the eye or lock of a layer does the same as a plain click: it toggles only that layer.

In Illustrator, Alt-clicking (Option-clicking) an eye shows or hides all the *other* items, and Alt-clicking a lock locks or unlocks all the others. Adobe's help ("Lock, hide, and delete objects") lists them as "Alt-click the eye icon next to a layer or item" and "Alt-click the lock icon". It's the usual way to isolate one layer while working.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make three layers, each with an object. Open the Layers panel.
2. Hold Alt and click Layer 2's eye.
3. Undo, then hold Alt and click Layer 2's lock.

**Actual result**
- Step 2 hides Layer 2 and leaves Layers 1 and 3 visible. History records "Layer Options".
- Step 3 locks Layer 2 only.

**Expected result**
- Step 2 hides Layers 1 and 3 and keeps Layer 2 visible. Alt-clicking again shows them all.
- Step 3 locks Layers 1 and 3 and leaves Layer 2 unlocked.

**Screenshot**
![After Alt-clicking Layer 2's eye in the Layers panel, Layer 2 is hidden and Layers 1 and 3 are still visible](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/layers-alt-eye.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/layers.rs`, `row`: the eye and lock columns check `clicked()` only and toggle that row through `layer.setProps` / `object.setProps`. Modifiers are never read. `object.setProps {ids, visible|locked}` already sets many nodes, layers included, in one undo step. A PR follows that makes Alt-click apply to the row's siblings: the other layers for a layer row, the other items in the same container for an object row.

Not in scope here: Ctrl-click on an eye (Outline view for one layer, which needs per-layer outline viewing), and dragging down the eye column to toggle several rows.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11, with real Alt+clicks.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Holding Space while drawing a shape doesn't move it; it keeps resizing
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Holding Space while drawing a shape doesn't move it. The shape keeps growing from where the drag started.

In Illustrator, holding Space during a Rectangle, Ellipse, Polygon, Star or Line Segment drag lets you reposition the shape you're drawing. It moves with the pointer at its current size, and releasing Space resumes sizing. Adobe's help on drawing rectangles and ellipses says to hold the spacebar while dragging to move the shape.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Choose the Rectangle tool.
2. Press at (50, 50) pt and drag to (150, 120) pt, so the rectangle is 100 × 70.
3. Keep the button down, hold Space and keep dragging to (250, 170). Release the button, then Space.

**Actual result**
The rectangle runs from (50, 50) to (250, 170), 200 × 120, as if Space weren't held. The size readout keeps growing during step 3.

**Expected result**
The 100 × 70 rectangle moves with the pointer during step 3 and ends from (150, 100) to (250, 170).

**Screenshot**
![Rectangle tool: after dragging to (150, 120) and holding Space while moving on to (250, 170), the rectangle still grows (W 200 pt, H 120 pt) instead of moving](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/space-move-shape.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/tools/src/shape.rs`, `ShapeTool::pointer`: the `Drag` arm always builds the shape from `self.start` to the pointer. `Mods` carries `space` (the canvas passes it with every drag event via `canvas::mods`), but the tool never reads it. A PR follows that moves the drag's start by the pointer's movement while Space is held. One change covers all six tools that share `ShapeTool`.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11, with a real mouse drag and the real Space key.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._
