title: Bug: Form dialogs open without a focused field: typing a value and pressing Enter applies the default
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
A form dialog such as Rotate, Scale, Move, Shear or Offset Path opens with no field focused. Typing a value right away goes nowhere. Pressing Enter then applies the dialog with its default value, which records a step that does nothing (a "Rotate" by 0°).

In Illustrator, a dialog opens with its first field focused and its contents selected. "Double-click the Rotate tool, type 45, press Enter" is a common keyboard-driven way to work.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Select an object.
2. Double-click the Rotate tool (or choose Object › Transform › Rotate…).
3. Type `30`, then press Enter.

**Actual result**
The dialog closes and History gains a "Rotate" step, but the object isn't rotated (`selectionRotation` stays 0). The Angle field never had the focus, so the 30 was never typed into it. To enter a value you first have to click the field.

**Expected result**
The Angle field is focused with "0" selected when the dialog opens. Typing `30` replaces it, and Enter rotates by 30°. The same goes for every form dialog's first field.

**Screenshot**
![The Rotate dialog just after opening: the Angle field shows 0 without focus or selection, so typed digits go nowhere](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/dialog-no-focus.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/mod.rs`, `show`, draws the form dialogs. Neither it nor the field helpers (`form::text_edit`, `widgets::num_field`) ever request focus. A PR follows that gives the first field the focus, with its text selected, on the frame a dialog opens.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11, with a real double-click and real typing.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Pen tool: pressing Alt mid-drag throws away the curve into the new point
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
With the Pen tool, pressing Alt while you're still dragging out a smooth point snaps that point's incoming handle onto the anchor. The curve you just shaped into the new point is lost: the segment becomes a straight line.

In Illustrator, Alt pressed mid-drag splits the direction lines. The incoming one stays where it was, and only the outgoing one follows the pointer. That's how Illustrator's help page [Draw two curved segments connected by a corner](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-two-curved-segments-connected-by-a-corner.html) draws a corner with curves on both sides.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Choose the Pen tool (P) and click once on the artboard.
2. Press the mouse a little further on and drag sideways, so that the new segment curves.
3. Without releasing the mouse button, press and hold Alt and keep dragging.

**Actual result**
As soon as Alt goes down, the curved segment turns into a straight line. The new anchor keeps only its outgoing handle. The committed path is `M0.5 50.348 L100.652 0.5`, a straight segment with no incoming handle.

**Expected result**
The curve stays as it was when Alt was pressed. The new anchor's incoming handle stays put, and the outgoing handle moves on its own and shapes the next segment.

**Screenshot**
![Top: dragging out a smooth point curves the new segment. Bottom: after pressing Alt mid-drag, the same segment is straight](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/pen-alt-mid-drag.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/tools/src/pen.rs`, the `PointerKind::Drag` arm: `let in_h = if alt { a } else { a - (out_h - a) };`. While Alt is held, the incoming handle is the anchor itself, whatever it was before Alt went down. A PR follows that keeps the incoming handle where it was when Alt went down. With Alt held from the start of the drag, that's still the anchor itself, as now.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11,…

title: Bug: Pen tool has no Auto Add/Delete on a selected path (the preference does nothing)

The Pen tool has no Auto Add/Delete. Over a segment of a selected path it should add an anchor there, and over one of its anchors it should delete it. Instead, it shows the plain Pen cursor and a click starts a new path on top of the selected one.

VectorCraft already has that preference (`disableAutoAddDelete`, labelled "Disable Auto Add/Delete"), but nothing reads it.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Draw an open path with three anchors and keep it selected.
2. Choose the Pen tool (P).
3. Point at the middle of one of its segments and click.
4. Undo, then click its middle anchor instead.

**Actual result**
- The cursor is the plain Pen with its new-path mark, over both the segment and the anchor.
- Each click starts a new path at the click point (`document.inspect` lists a new one-anchor path). The selected path keeps its 3 anchors.

**Expected result**

- The ends of a selected open path still continue it, and Shift or the preference turns the switching off.

title: Bug: Pen tool: holding Space while dragging out a point doesn't move it
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
With the Pen tool, holding Space while still dragging out a new point doesn't move that point. The anchor stays where the button went down, and the drag keeps reshaping its handles around it.

In Illustrator, holding the spacebar while the mouse button is still down moves the anchor being placed, with its handles. Releasing Space goes back to shaping the handles. 2. Press the mouse a little further on and drag sideways to pull out handles.

The anchor stays where the button went down. While Space is held, the handles swing round it to follow the pointer. title: Bug: Pen tool: clicking the last anchor adds a duplicate point (and a spike) instead of retracting its handle

body:

While drawing with the Pen tool, clicking the last anchor you placed adds a second anchor at the same spot. In Illustrator, the Pen over the last anchor of the path being drawn shows a convert mark. A click retracts that anchor's outgoing handle, so the next segment leaves it as a corner and the curve into it stays. A drag pulls a new outgoing handle out on its own, setting the slope of the next curve. See Illustrator's help pages [Draw curves and straight lines](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-curves-followed-by-straight-lines.html) (the click) and [Draw straight lines and curves with Pen tool](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/draw-shapes-and-paths/draw-shapes/draw-straight-lines-followed-by-curves.html) (the drag).

1. Choose the Pen tool (P) and click once on the artboard.
2. Press further on and drag sideways to place a smooth point, then release.
3. Click that same smooth point again.
4. Click a third point elsewhere, then press Enter.

**Actual result**
- After step 3 the path has 3 anchors, and after step 4 it has 4. Two of them are at the same spot.
- The SVG shows the degenerate segment `C150.728 0.5 100.652 0.5 100.652 0.5` between them, which draws as a spike next to the point.

- Dragging from the last anchor instead pulls out a new outgoing handle without changing the incoming one.

title: Bug: PDF import ignores embedded fonts: text whose font isn't installed is re-set and exported in the fallback font (also with textAs: outlines), without an export warning
author: zfxxvjpcd6-afk
body:
**Version:** v0.4.0, `vectorcraft-0.4.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (SHA256 matches `SHA256SUMS.txt`), `vectorcraft-cli`, headless, no fonts installed besides the bundled ones.

### What happens

When a PDF embeds a font program (subset TrueType here) that isn't installed, the import sets the text in the fallback font, **Source Sans 3**, and every export writes that fallback font. The embedded font program in the file is never used:

- `vectorcraft-cli info repro.pdf` reports `"family": "Deja Vu Serif Condensed", "status": "missing", "resolved": {"family": "Source Sans 3"}`.
- `vectorcraft-cli convert repro.pdf out.pdf` writes the text as outlines of **Source Sans 3**, so serif becomes sans and the line width changes. The result is `"warnings": []`.
- `document.exportPdf {"advanced": {"outlineText": false}}` embeds `SourceSans3-Regular` instead of the original font (`pdffonts`). The result is again `"warnings": []`.
- `document.open {"textAs": "outlines"}` gives the same result. I expected `textAs: "outlines"` to keep the file's own glyph outlines, because the glyphs are in the file.

Opening does warn: "fonts that aren't available show in the fallback font until they are". The export does not mention it, though, and in a headless batch the substitution ends up silently in the output file.

**Real-world impact:** print-ready PDF/X files from Illustrator usually embed fonts that are licensed only on the designer's machine, such as Adobe Fonts. A round trip through VectorCraft then re-flows every text: on a 2-page PDF/X-3 packaging file, text ran out of its background and under a barcode.

### Expected

1. If the PDF embeds the font program, use it for rendering and for `textAs: "outlines"`. At minimum, use it for text the user doesn't edit.
2. Otherwise, report the substitution in the export result's `warnings` as well, not only when opening.

title: Bug: PDF round trip writes DeviceCMYK images as RGB (default export: DeviceRGB, PDF/X-3: ICC RGB) without a warning
author: zfxxvjpcd6-afk
body:
**Version:** v0.4.0, `vectorcraft-0.4.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `vectorcraft-cli`, headless.

### What happens

A PDF with a **DeviceCMYK image** opens as a CMYK document (`info` → `"colorMode": "cmyk"`). The exports don't keep the image in CMYK, and none of them warns:

| Export | Image colour space in the output (pikepdf) | `warnings` |
|---|---|---|
| `vectorcraft-cli convert repro.pdf out.pdf` | `/DeviceRGB` | `[]` |
| `document.exportPdf {"standard": "pdfX3"}` | `/ICCBased`, **N=3** (RGB); output intent `VectorCraft Generic CMYK (SWOP-like)` | `[]` |

The DeviceCMYK vector fill in the same file stays CMYK, so only images are affected. The rendered colour of the image shifts slightly as well (poppler, sRGB patch mean 252,212,146 → 254,216,162).

On a real 2-page PDF/X-3 print file with 229 DeviceCMYK JPEG tiles I saw the same thing: all tiles came out RGB in the default export and ICC-RGB in PDF/X-3. With `output: {"conversion": "preserveNumbers"}` they stayed CMYK (ICC N=4). With `pdfX1a` they were DeviceCMYK again, but with changed values: in a sample patch, C, M and Y moved by about 1–3.5 percentage points.

### Expected

`docs/mcp.md` says "Imported colours keep their model: DeviceCMYK and CMYK ICC colours stay CMYK". For a print workflow (open a PDF/X file, change a text, export PDF/X again), I'd expect:

1. DeviceCMYK images in a CMYK document are written as CMYK by default, with their original values, and ideally passed through unchanged when the image itself isn't edited.
2. If an export does convert them, it says so in `warnings`.
3. Optional: when the source file has an output intent, it is kept as the default for PDF/X exports instead of the generic SWOP-like profile.

title: .ai import: a page-sized white fill outside every layer comes in as art (a "Page 1" layer behind the artwork)
author: EthanSuquet
body:
**Version:** `main` at 0d4d125, `vectorcraft-cli` (headless), macOS 26.6, M2 Max.

### What happens

Opening a PDF-compatible `.ai` whose PDF part paints a white rectangle over the whole page **outside its optional-content layers**, and then the layers' art, gives the document an extra layer named "Page 1" holding a page-sized white path, under the file's own layers.

On real files saved by the reference app (version 30, one artboard, one layer), the PDF part starts with exactly such a fill (`/CS0 cs 1 1 1 scn 0 h w -h re f`, before the first `/OC /MC0 BDC`). The EPS saved from the same artwork has 15 paths and no background; the `.ai` opens with 16, the extra one being this fill.

The page fill isn't part of any layer, so it isn't artwork: the file opens with only its layers (as the EPS of the same artwork does), with a transparent background. title: Bug: Left/Right arrows don't change grid columns while dragging a Rectangular or Polar Grid
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
While dragging out a Rectangular Grid or a Polar Grid, the Left and Right arrow keys do nothing. Up and Down change the rows (concentric dividers) as they should, but Left/Right never change the columns (radial dividers).

The grid tools are written to take them. The doc of `crates/tools/src/draw2/family.rs` says "←/→ change grid columns / radial dividers", and `FamilyTool::key` handles `ToolKey::Left` / `ToolKey::Right`. In Illustrator, the arrow keys add or remove the grid's lines as you drag, Left/Right for the vertical (radial) ones.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Choose the Rectangular Grid tool and start dragging on the artboard.
2. Without releasing the button, press Up three times: three rows are added.
3. Start another grid and press Right three times while dragging.

**Actual result**
Right (and Left) change nothing: the grid keeps 5 vertical dividers. The same goes for the Polar Grid's radial dividers.

**Expected result**
Right adds a column (a radial divider) and Left removes one, live in the preview, like Up/Down for rows.

**Screenshot**
![A Rectangular Grid drag: Up pressed three times adds three rows, Right pressed three times leaves the columns unchanged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/grid-arrows.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`: while the active tool is busy (a drag in progress), only `ArrowUp` and `ArrowDown` (and digits) are passed to the tool (`for (k, tk) in [(Key::ArrowUp, ToolKey::Up), (Key::ArrowDown, ToolKey::Down)]`), so Left/Right are dropped. A PR follows.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11, with real mouse and keyboard input.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: New sublayers are named after the object count ("Layer 1" in an empty document), and new layers can repeat their names
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
A new sublayer is named after the number of objects in the document, not the number of layers.
- In an empty document, Create New Sublayer gives "Layer 1", the same name as its parent.
- In a document with five objects, it gives "Layer 6".
- A new top-level layer only looks at top-level names, so it can reuse a sublayer's name. With five objects, Create New Sublayer then Create New Layer give "Layer 6" and then "Layer 2".

In Illustrator, layers and sublayers share one numbering. Layer 1, then a new sublayer, then a new layer give "Layer 2" and then "Layer 3", whatever art the document holds.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. File › New. In the Layers panel, click Create New Sublayer (the "+" button at the bottom).
2. In a new document, draw five rectangles, then click Create New Sublayer and then Create New Layer.

**Actual result**
- Step 1: the sublayer is "Layer 1", like its parent.
- Step 2: the sublayer is "Layer 6" and the new layer is "Layer 2".

**Expected result**
- Step 1: "Layer 2".
- Step 2: "Layer 2" for the sublayer, then "Layer 3" for the new layer. No two layers share a default name.

**Screenshot**
![The Layers panel: an empty document's new sublayer is named "Layer 1" like its parent; with five rectangles a new sublayer is "Layer 6" and a later new layer "Layer 2"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/layer-names-bug.png)

**Where it comes from**
- `crates/engine/src/cmd/layer.rs`, `new_sublayer`: `format!("Layer {}", d.node_count())`. `Document::node_count` counts every node, art included.
- `crates/doc/src/lib.rs`, `Document::next_layer_name`, used for top-level layers: it starts at the number of top-level layers + 1 and skips only top-level names, so a sublayer's name can come back.

A PR follows.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11, with real mouse input.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Layers panel: a row can't be dropped into another layer (nothing happens on an empty layer)
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
In the Layers panel, dragging an object's row onto another layer's row doesn't move the object into that layer. The drop line only ever goes above or below a row. A row of a top-level layer offers nowhere an object can go (art can't sit between layers), so the drop does nothing. An object can't be dragged into an empty layer at all, and a layer can't be dragged into another to make it a sublayer.

In Illustrator, dropping a row onto a layer's row (the row highlights) moves the object into that layer, on top of its contents. Dropping on the gap between rows still reorders.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Draw a rectangle, then click Create New Layer in the Layers panel. The new layer is empty, on top.
2. Drag the rectangle's row onto the middle of the new layer's row and release.

**Actual result**
A drop line shows along the new layer's bottom edge, and on release nothing changes: the rectangle stays in Layer 1 and History gains no step. The same happens wherever on the row it's dropped.

**Expected result**
The new layer's row highlights while hovered, and the rectangle moves into it on release. A layer dropped the same way onto another layer becomes its sublayer. Dropping near a row's top or bottom edge still places the row above or below.

**Screenshot**
![Layers panel: dragging a Rectangle row onto the empty Layer 3 shows a line under Layer 3; after release the rectangle is still in Layer 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/layers-drop-into.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/layers.rs`, `row`, the "Drag to reorder" block. The drop is "above" or "below" the hovered row in that row's parent. For a top-level layer row the parent is `None`, which only layers may use, so a dragged object is skipped. There's no "into this row" case. A PR follows. (Illustrator's other way, dragging the selected-art square to another layer, isn't covered here.)

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windo…

title: Bug: Artboard tool: Alt-drag moves the artboard instead of duplicating it
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
With the Artboard tool, Alt-dragging an artboard moves it like a plain drag. No copy is made and the original doesn't stay where it was.

In Illustrator, Alt-dragging an artboard with the Artboard tool duplicates it. The copy follows the pointer, and with Move/Copy Artwork with Artboard on, its artwork is copied too. See Illustrator's help page [Duplicate artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/duplicate-artboards.html).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. New document (200 × 150 pt) with a rectangle on the artboard.
2. Choose the Artboard tool (Shift+O), hold Alt and drag from inside the artboard 220 pt to the right, then release.

**Actual result**
The document still has one artboard, now at x = 220, and the rectangle moved with it. History says "Move Artboard".

**Expected result**
Two artboards: "Artboard 1" still at x = 0 with its rectangle, and a copy at x = 220 with a copy of the rectangle. History says "Duplicate Artboard".

**Screenshot**
![Before: one artboard with a blue rectangle. After an Alt-drag to the right with the Artboard tool: the same single artboard moved, no copy left behind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/artboard-alt-drag.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/tools/src/xform/artboard.rs`: the `Drag::Move` arm never reads Alt (Alt only resizes from the centre on a handle), and `artboard.move` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/xform.rs`) has no copy mode. `artboard.duplicate` exists but always places the copy right of the last artboard, without its art. A PR follows.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11, with real mouse and keyboard input.

_Found while testing VectorCraft with Claude Code._

title: Bug: Clicking an artboard in the Artboards panel doesn't make it active (Fit Artboard in Window still fits the old one)
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Clicking an artboard in the Artboards panel only highlights its row. It doesn't make that artboard the active one, so the status bar's artboard navigator stays where it was, and View › Fit Artboard in Window (Ctrl+0) and Actual Size still show the previous artboard.

In Illustrator, selecting an artboard's name in the Artboards panel makes it the active artboard. See Illustrator's help page [Select artboards](https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/desktop/create-manage-artboards/add-edit-artboards/select-artboards.html).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. New document with two artboards (Artboard 2 elsewhere on the canvas).
2. Window › Artboards, click "Artboard 2".
3. View › Fit Artboard in Window (Ctrl+0).

**Actual result**
- The panel highlights Artboard 2, but the status bar navigator still reads 1.
- Ctrl+0 fits Artboard 1: the view's `artboard` stays 0 and its centre stays at Artboard 1's.

**Expected result**
Clicking Artboard 2 makes it active: the navigator reads 2, and Fit Artboard in Window and Actual Size work on Artboard 2. The navigator and the panel always show the same artboard.

**Screenshot**
![After clicking Artboard 2 in the Artboards panel, Ctrl+0 fits Artboard 1, and the status bar's navigator still shows artboard 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/artboards-panel-active.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/artboards.rs`: a row click only stores the panel's own selection (`pstate "ab-sel"`), which nothing outside the panel reads. The active artboard the navigator and the Fit/Actual Size commands use is the document view's `artboard` index (`state::View::artboard`, set by `view.goToArtboard`). A PR follows.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11, with real mouse input.

title: Bug: Up/Down arrows don't step the value in panel number fields (W, H, X, Y, stroke weight…)
author: theironchef
body:

In Illustrator, with a numeric field focused, Up/Down raise or lower the value by 1 unit, Shift+Up/Down by 10, and Ctrl (Cmd)+Up/Down by a fraction, and the change applies at once. **Steps to reproduce**
1. Draw a 100 × 50 pt rectangle and keep it selected.
2. In the Properties panel, click into W.
3. Press Up three times, then Shift+Up, then Enter.

**Actual result**
W stays 100 pt throughout. The field keeps the focus, nothing reaches the rectangle, and History shows no change.

**Expected result**
W goes 101, 102, 103 pt and then 113 pt, the rectangle following each step.

**Screenshot**
![The Properties panel's W field focused after pressing Up three times: it still reads 100 pt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/num-field-arrows.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/widgets.rs`, `num_field`: the field only parses its text on Enter or focus loss. Nothing reads the arrow keys while it has focus. A PR follows.

File opens

title: Bug: Pressing Tab leaves the keyboard on a hidden field, so a second Tab, tool letters, Ctrl chords and Type tool typing stop working
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
Pressing Tab hides the panels, but it also leaves the keyboard focus on a field that isn't visible. From then on every key counts as typing in a field, so tool letters, Ctrl chords and a second Tab do nothing until you click the canvas or press Esc. In the Type tool, Tab types a tab character and the letter typed right after it is lost.

In Illustrator, Tab shows and hides the panels (Window › Panels) and nothing else: the keys after it work as before.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document and click the canvas, so no field has the keyboard. Press Tab: the panels hide.
2. Press Tab again.
3. Press P (the Pen tool's shortcut), or Ctrl+A with an object on the artboard.
4. Choose the Type tool, click the canvas, type `a`, press Tab, type `b`.

**Actual result**
- Step 2: the panels stay hidden.
- Step 3: the tool doesn't change, and Ctrl+A selects nothing. Esc or a click on the canvas gets the keys back, for the next key.
- Step 4: the text is "a" followed by a tab; the `b` never arrives.

**Expected result**
- A second Tab shows the panels again.
- P and Ctrl+A work after Tab.
- The Type tool's text is "a", a tab and "b".

**Screenshot**
![After Tab, Tab and P the status bar still names the Selection tool; in the Type tool, typing a, Tab and b leaves only the a and the tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/tab-key-bug.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`: the Tab shortcut (`window.dock`) is taken from the frame's input, but egui's own focus navigation has already read the same Tab press at the start of the frame, and it moves the keyboard focus to the first field (`Memory::move_focus`). `ctx.egui_wants_keyboard_input()` is then true, and `handle` returns early ("typing") for every later key. A PR follows that cancels the focus move when no field has the keyboard.

**Environment**
- Release build of `main` on Windows 11, with real keyboard input.

title: [Bug] Recovery discard removes a still-open tab’s snapshot after heartbeat expiry
author: Jagalite
body:
A second browser tab can discard the recovery snapshot of a still-live document after its owner tab stops running timers long enough for the heartbeat to expire. The original tab can resume and save its intact edited document, but its recovery snapshot has already been removed.

## Environment

- Current main `5cacbe36b33608c8803e03f25a1178354218f9a0`, fresh release browser build; Rust 1.95.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.129, `?webgl`.
- macOS 26.5.2 arm64, Apple M1; isolated headless Chrome 154.0.8037.93 and Playwright WebKit 26.6 (not Safari).

## Reproduction

Use two tabs A and B sharing the same origin and localStorage. Before app startup in A, instrument its `requestAnimationFrame`, `setTimeout` and `setInterval` callbacks so they can be paused without closing the page. The controlled run queued animation and timeout callbacks while paused, skipped interval callbacks, and allowed them to resume afterward. This is synthetic timer suspension, not physical operating-system suspension.

1. In A, open a 200×200 SVG with four named paths: `red`, `blue`, `circle`, `curve`. Delete `red` without saving the document.
2. Set Preferences → File Handling/Data Recovery to one minute. Run `file.recovery.save` through the command palette.
3. Inspect `vectorcraft-recovery/<owner>/` in localStorage. Confirm that the native snapshot contains exactly `blue`, `circle`, `curve` and has a current heartbeat.
4. Open B, also set one-minute recovery, and run `file.recovery.discard`. As a healthy control, verify A's current-owner snapshot remains present.
5. Pause A's timers and animation callbacks while retaining its open page and document. Wait 186 real seconds in B, beyond the three-minute heartbeat threshold.
6. Run `file.recovery.discard` in B again and inspect A's recovery keys.
7. Resume A, save its actual native document, and independently inspect the saved JSON.

2. Choose the Scale tool (S). Hold Alt, press the mouse button beside the rectangle and drag 100 pt to the right, then release.
3. Repeat with Rotate (R), Reflect (O) and Shear.

**Actual result**
The Scale dialog opens on the press, with its origin at the press point, and the drag does nothing. The rectangle is unchanged, and the document still has one object. Rotate, Reflect and Shear open their dialogs the same way.

**Expected result**
- Alt held and dragged: a transformed copy is made, and the original stays (the dialog's "Copy" does the same by hand).

title: Bug: Rotate, Reflect, Scale and Shear tools: Enter doesn't open the dialog
author: theironchef
body:
**Description**
With the Rotate, Reflect, Scale or Shear tool chosen and something selected, pressing Enter does nothing. The tools are meant to open their dialog from Enter, at the reference point (the selection's centre, or the point set with a click): the module doc of `crates/tools/src/xform/transform.rs` says "double-click or Return opens the dialog too", and the tool's unit test checks the `Dialog` action. A double-click on the tool's button works (#264); Enter doesn't.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Draw a rectangle and keep it selected.
2. Choose the Rotate tool (R).
3. Press Enter. Setting the reference point with a click first makes no difference.
4. Repeat with Reflect (O), Scale (S) and Shear (no shortcut: pick it from the toolbar).
5. For comparison, double-click the Rotate tool's button.

**Actual result**
Steps 3 and 4: nothing happens, no dialog. Step 5: the Rotate dialog opens.

**Expected result**
Enter opens the tool's dialog, as the double-click does.

**Screenshot**
![Rotate tool chosen and a rectangle selected: Enter opens no dialog, a double-click on the tool's button opens the Rotate dialog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/theironchef/vectorcraft/issue-screenshots/transform-enter-missing.png)

**Where it comes from**
`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs`, `handle`: the Enter and Escape loop gets what the tool asks of the UI back from `tool_key` (`TransformTool::key` answers Enter with `Action::Dialog`, which arrives as `UiRequest::Dialog`), but applies it only `if claimed`, that is for a key the tool claims ahead of the shortcuts (Esc with the place cursor loaded). For any other key, including this Enter, the request is dropped. The tool-level test never goes through the UI, so it passes. A dialog opened by the key also has to consume it: dialogs take Enter as OK in the same frame. A PR follows.

title: Bug: Cmd+A in a text field or in text being edited selects every object instead of the text
author: houseoftag
body:
**Description**
Ctrl+A (Cmd+A on macOS) always runs Select › All and selects every object in the document, even when the keyboard is in a text field. In a panel or dialog field it should select all the text in that field. While editing type on the canvas it should select all the text in the frame being edited.

In Illustrator, Cmd+A in a field selects the field's text, and Cmd+A while editing type selects all the text in the story. Select › All runs only when no text has the keyboard.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Open a document with a few objects.
2. Click into a panel field, e.g. W in Properties, and press Cmd+A.
3. Press Esc. With the Type tool, click into a text frame so the caret shows, and press Cmd+A.

**Actual result**
- Step 2: every object on the artboard is selected. The field's text is not selected.
- Step 3: every object on the artboard is selected. The text in the frame is not selected.

**Expected result**
- Step 2: all the text in the W field is selected, and the object selection doesn't change.
- Step 3: all the text in the frame (the story) is selected, ready to type over or restyle.

**Where it comes from**
- macOS, fields: `apps/vectorcraft/src/native_menu.rs` (`accel`, lines 37–43) turns every shortcut with Cmd, Ctrl or Alt into a native menu accelerator, `select.all` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/select.rs:12`) included. The system menu takes the chord before egui sees it, and `NativeMenu::poll` (lines 76–81) calls `menus::invoke`, which checks `waits_for_ime` but not `egui_wants_keyboard_input()`. So the key never reaches the focused `TextEdit`. The comment at lines 35–36 guards only keys without modifiers. title: Bug: SVG import: text under a transform or viewBox scale shows its SVG font-size in the Character panel but draws at a different size

**Description**
When an SVG's text sits under a scale (a `transform` on the `<text>`, a `transform` on a parent `<g>`, or a `viewBox` that differs from `width`/`height`), the imported text keeps the SVG's nominal `font-size` as its size and carries the scale in the object's transform. The Character panel then shows that nominal size, but the text draws at size × scale. Two objects can both read 7 pt and look very different, and setting 7 pt again changes nothing.

In Illustrator the drawn size always matches the size the Character panel shows, and SVG text under a scale opens with the scale applied to its size (unverified on this exact file).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Save this as `t.svg` and open it (File › Open):

title: Type: defaults for new Japanese type — leading model and character alignment (#385, #389 follow-up)

#385 added the leading model (Roman baseline / em-box top-to-top) and #389 character alignment, both as opt-in settings: new type keeps the Roman-baseline defaults, so nothing changes for existing documents or for Latin text.

The question is what VectorCraft's defaults for *new* type should be, in particular whether Japanese type should start with **em-box top-to-top** leading and **em-box centre** character alignment. Options I see:

title: macOS 27: `opened_files_wait_for_the_ui` fails — an https NSURL comes back as a file path
author: imachus
body:
On macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), `cargo test -p vectorcraft` fails in `apps/vectorcraft/src/open_documents.rs`:

```
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: ["/tmp/a b.pdf", "/a.svg", "/tmp/c.ai"]
 right: ["/tmp/a b.pdf", "/tmp/c.ai"]
```

`NSURL::to_file_path()` returns `Some("/a.svg")` for `https://example.com/a.svg` on this system, so `open_urls` queues a web URL's path as if it were a file. It happens without any local changes (main as of today).

A possible fix is to keep only file URLs before converting, e.g. `urls.iter().filter(|u| u.isFileURL()).filter_map(|u| u.to_file_path())`. Happy to send a PR if that's the way you'd like it fixed.

title: Shape Builder is missing the erase tool (negative modifier)
author: lostdesign
body:
## Feature Request

The Shape Builder tool currently supports merging shapes but is missing the **Erase Mode** available in Adobe Illustrator, which allows users to subtract or remove regions directly within the Shape Builder tool.

### Expected Behavior

Adobe Illustrator's Shape Builder supports two modes:

- **Merge Mode (default):** Click or drag across overlapping regions to combine them into a single shape.
- **Erase Mode (Alt/Option):** Hold `Alt` (Windows/Linux) or `Option` (macOS) to temporarily switch to Erase Mode and remove unwanted regions.

Erase Mode allows users to:
- Delete individual regions by clicking them.
- Remove multiple regions by dragging across them.
- Remove shared regions from overlapping shapes, splitting the affected paths appropriately.
- Delete edges and remaining unwanted path segments.

### Proposed Implementation

Add an Erase Mode to VectorCraft's Shape Builder that:

- Activates while holding `Alt` / `Option`.
- Supports removing regions through clicking and dragging.
- Correctly updates the underlying paths when removing overlapping regions.
- Allows removing edges as well as filled regions.
- Provides visual feedback indicating which regions will be deleted.
- Automatically switches back to Merge Mode when the modifier is released.

This would allow users to seamlessly switch between adding and subtracting regions without leaving the Shape Builder tool.

### Reference

Adobe Illustrator documents this functionality under **Erase Mode** in its official Shape Builder documentation:

https://helpx.adobe.com/illustrator/using/creating-shapes-shape-builder-tool.html

Thank you!

title: [Bug] [macOS] VectorCraft v0.4.0 missing from "Open With" menu & fails to open files from Finder
author: PercyMichael
body:
## Description
On macOS, VectorCraft (`v0.4.0`) does not appear in Finder's **"Open With"** contextual menu when right-clicking vector files (`.svg`, `.ai`, `.eps`, `.vectorcraft`). If forced to open via **"Open With > Other..."**, VectorCraft launches but fails to load the file into the editor.

*Note: Opening the exact same file **internally** using the "Open" button inside VectorCraft works without any issues.*

## Environment
- **OS:** macOS Monterey 12.7.4 (Build 21H1123)
- **App Version:** VectorCraft v0.4.0 (`/Applications/VectorCraft.app`)
- **File Extension(s) Tested:** `.svg`, `.ai`, `.eps`, `.vectorcraft`

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In macOS Finder, right-click any vector file (e.g. `design.svg` or `project.vectorcraft`).
2. Inspect the **"Open With"** context menu:
   - **Result:** VectorCraft is **not listed** as a recommended application.
3. Select **"Open With > Other..."**, choose `/Applications/VectorCraft.app`, and click **Open**.
   - **Result:** VectorCraft launches, but opens to a blank workspace without loading the selected file.
4. Inside VectorCraft, click the internal **"Open"** button/menu and select the file.
   - **Result:** The file **loads successfully** inside the app canvas.

## Expected Behavior
1. VectorCraft should automatically appear in macOS Finder's **"Open With"** menu for `.svg`, `.ai`, `.eps`, and `.vectorcraft` files.
2. Selecting VectorCraft from Finder (or double-clicking an associated file) should launch the app and open the file directly in the editor.

## Confirmed Root Cause & Technical Details

title: Keyboard Shortcuts editor records the modifier keydown as the chord — no modified chord can be recorded
author: ktheunlikedoll
body:
VectorCraft 0.4.0 — Linux x86_64 (RPM), KDE Plasma, Wayland

### Steps to reproduce
1. Edit → Keyboard Shortcuts
2. Click the shortcut cell of any entry (e.g. the Group Selection tool) — the cell shows "Press keys…"
3. Press `Shift+A` (or `Cmd+K`, or any chord that starts with a modifier)

### Actual
The recording ends on the modifier keydown and the binding is saved as a modifier-only chord — `ShiftLeft` (or `Shift+ShiftLeft`, depending on the modifiers snapshot), `ControlLeft`, etc. The second key is never captured. The saved chord parses fine but can never fire, and the entry keeps a dead override until it's cleared by hand.

### Expected
Modifier presses should be held as prefix keys while recording; the chord completes on the first non-modifier key (Esc cancels).

### Cause
egui 0.36 emits physical `Event::Key` presses for modifier keys (`Key::ShiftLeft`/`ShiftRight`/`ControlLeft`/… — "these variants are emitted only as physical Event::Key presses", [egui 0.36.2 `crates/egui/src/data/key.rs`](https://github.com/emilk/egui/blob/0.36.2/crates/egui/src/data/key.rs)). The recorder in [`crates/ui-egui/src/shortcut_editor.rs`](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/main/crates/ui-egui/src/shortcut_editor.rs) takes the first `pressed` `Event::Key` via `find_map` without filtering modifier variants:

```rust
let ev = ctx.input(|i| {
    i.events.iter().find_map(|e| match e {
        egui::Event::Key { key, pressed: true, modifiers, .. } => Some((*key, *modifiers)),
        _ => None,
    })
});
```

`format`/`parse` accept the result because `Key::from_name("ShiftLeft")` resolves, so the dead chord is assigned and persisted to `ui.json` (`shortcut_overrides`).

Notably this also breaks legal Shift-only tool chords (e.g. trying to set a tool to `Shift+A`), not just Cmd/Ctrl/Alt combos.

### Suggested fix
In the recorder, ignore `Event::Key` where the key is one of the modifier variants (ShiftLeft/Right, ControlLeft/Right, AltLeft/Right, SuperLeft/Right) so record…

2026-10-08T13:27:05.487Z INFO  [main] vectorcraft: rendering with AMD Ryzen 9 7900X 12-Core Processor (RADV RAPHAEL_MENDOCINO) (Vulkan, IntegratedGpu) (power preference LowPower)

title: SVG round trip drops display="none" groups and data-* attributes
author: cranberrylettuce
body:
**Version:** vectorcraft-cli 0.6.0 (macOS universal)

## What happens

`vectorcraft-cli convert in.svg out.svg` on an SVG used as an animation rig (hidden alternate shapes plus pivot points stored as attributes):

1. Groups with `display="none"` are imported (they show up as `visible: false` in the `.vectorcraft` file, and `info` counts them), but the SVG exporter omits invisible objects. On our real rig (230 objects, 61 ids) 28 ids are lost.
2. `data-*` attributes (e.g. `data-pivot="100,180"`) are dropped on import, and no command can set them (`object.setProps` takes only name/visible/locked/opacity/blend/knockout).

Running `object.showAll` before export keeps the ids, but then every alternate renders at once and the hidden state is gone.

## Why it matters

SVG character rigs keep alternate expressions/hands as hidden groups and their rotation anchors as `data-*` attributes. The round trip silently breaks them.

## Repro

`rig-repro.svg`:

```svg
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 200 200" width="200" height="200">
  <g id="character" data-pivot="100,180">
    <g id="arm" data-pivot="60,100">
      <path d="M40 100 L60 90 L80 110 Z" fill="#b5835a"/>
    </g>
    <g id="arm-raised" data-pivot="60,100" display="none">
      <path d="M40 100 L50 60 L70 70 Z" fill="#b5835a"/>
    </g>
    <g id="eye-closed" display="none">
      <path d="M90 80 Q100 90 110 80" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="3"/>
    </g>
  </g>
</svg>
```

```
vectorcraft-cli convert rig-repro.svg out.svg
```

Expected: `arm-raised` and `eye-closed` still present with `display="none"`, and `data-pivot` on `character`, `arm`, `arm-raised`.
Actual: only `character` and `arm` are written, with no `data-pivot`.

## Suggested

- An export option (or default) that writes hidden objects with `display="none"`.
- Keep unknown/`data-*` attributes on import and write them back on export, ideally settable via `object.setProps`.

title: fix(cli): .ai is writable through file.saveAs but refused by --export and convert
author: Oldrich333
body:
> Agent-written on behalf of @Oldrich333 · agent: hive-admin/main · model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · origin: owner-requested

## Summary
VectorCraft 0.5.0 writes `.ai` through `file.saveAs` / `file.save` (`format: "ai"`), but the CLI export routes refuse the same format: `run … --export x.ai` and `convert in.svg out.ai` fail with "PDF-compatible .ai files can be opened but not written". The CLI usage text lists `.ai` as readable only. Two code paths disagree, so an agent that reads `--help` concludes `.ai` cannot be written, and one that reads the command params concludes `--export` should work.

## Runtime or environment
- VectorCraft 0.5.0 release (`vectorcraft-0.5.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, SHA256 verified), `vectorcraft-cli`, headless, Linux x86_64.

## Steps to reproduce
```sh
vectorcraft-cli run --cmd file.new --cmd file.saveAs --params '{"path":"/abs/t1.ai","format":"ai"}'
vectorcraft-cli info /abs/t1.ai
vectorcraft-cli run --cmd file.new --export t2.ai
vectorcraft-cli convert in.svg out.ai
vectorcraft-cli --help
```

## Expected behavior
One answer everywhere: if `.ai` is writable (as `file.saveAs` shows), `--export` and `convert` write it and `--help` lists it under writable formats; if it is not meant to be writable, `file.saveAs` refuses it and the `format` enum of `file.saveAs`/`document.save` drops `ai`.

## Actual behavior
- `file.saveAs` → `{"bytes":4011,"format":"ai","path":"/abs/t1.ai","warnings":[]}`; `info` and `run --in t1.ai` reopen it (`"restored":true,"format":"ai"`).
- `--export t2.ai` and `convert in.svg out.ai` → `vectorcraft-cli: export out.ai: invalid parameters for document.export: PDF-compatible .ai files can be opened but not written (see document.formats)`, exit 1, no file.
- `--help`: "Writable formats: .vectorcraft, .svg, .svgz, .pdf, .png, .jpg, .gif, .webp, .tif, .bmp, .vctemplate, .txt, .dxf, .eps, .emf, .wmf, .tga, .psd" (no `.ai`).

## Notes
Related: #372 (full .ai support), PR #79 (Save As .ai).

body:
**Version / platform:** VectorCraft v0.4.0 on macOS 26.7.1

**What I expected (Illustrator behaviour)**
1. Select two or more objects.
2. Click once more, without modifiers, on one of the selected objects.
3. That object becomes the key object (thick outline), and Align switches to "Align to Key Object".
4. Align buttons move the other objects to the key; the key does not move. Distribute Spacing uses the spacing value in the panel.
5. Clicking the key again, or Align panel menu › Cancel Key Object, clears it.

- `crates/tools/src/select.rs`: the press handler on a selected object (non-Shift) never sends `select.key`.

- `crates/engine/src/cmd/object.rs`: `reference_rect` already handles `to: "key"`.

**Suggested fix**
In the Selection tool, a press and release with no drag on an object that is already in a multi-object selection should send `select.key {id}` and set Align To to Key. Draw the key with a thicker selection outline. Clicking the key again should clear it.

title: Publish Vectorcraft (and the rest of the Artcraft suite) on Flathub
author: lucasgabmoreno
body:
Hi! Thanks for building Vectorcraft.

I noticed the releases page already includes a Flatpak bundle. Would you consider publishing the app on Flathub? It would make installation and automatic updates much easier for Linux users, and it would give the project more visibility.

It would also be great to see the other apps in the Artcraft suite (PhotoCraft,VectorCraft,FilmCraft,LightCraft,PdfCraft,EffectCraft,DesignCraft) published on Flathub the same way. Having the whole suite in one place would make it much easier for people to discover and install everything together.

Since the apps are written in Rust, the Flathub manifests would build from source using the Freedesktop SDK with the rust-stable extension. Cargo dependencies are handled with flatpak-cargo-generator, which generates a cargo-sources.json file so the build works offline.

What's needed on the project side, for each app:
- A valid app ID (e.g. io.github.storytold.Vectorcraft)
- An AppStream metainfo.xml file (description, screenshots, license, release notes)
- A .desktop file and an icon
- A manifest, which can likely be adapted from the one used to produce the current Flatpak bundle

Submission guide: [https://docs.flathub.org/docs/for-app-authors/submission](https://docs.flathub.org/docs/for-app-authors/submission)

I'd be happy to help with the manifests or testing if that would be useful. Thanks!

title: Linux/Wayland: app stops responding while File → Open dialog is open (compositor shows "Application not responding")
author: aravind-r2r-tech
body:
**Environment**
- VectorCraft 0.7.0, built from source via AUR `vectorcraft`
- Arch Linux (Omarchy), Hyprland 0.56.2, Wayland
- xdg-desktop-portal-gtk for file dialogs
- Intel HD Graphics 4600 (Haswell), running on the GL backend

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Launch VectorCraft.
2. File → Open.
3. Leave the file chooser open while browsing (e.g. into ~/Downloads) for a few seconds.

**Expected:** the main window keeps responding while the file chooser is open.

**Actual:** the main window stops answering the Wayland `xdg_wm_base` ping for as long as the chooser is open. Hyprland shows "Application not responding — Wait / Terminate" after its threshold (~4.5 s with the default `misc:anr_missed_pings`). Choosing Terminate SIGKILLs the app, so it looks like a crash to users who browse for more than a few seconds. Choosing Wait works, and the app resumes once the chooser closes.

This suggests the file dialog is awaited synchronously on the event-loop thread (e.g. a blocking `rfd::FileDialog`). Using `rfd::AsyncFileDialog`, or running the dialog off the main thread while the event loop keeps pumping, should fix it.

**Also logged:** each time the dialog opens, `xdg-desktop-portal-gtk` reports `Unhandled parent window type` and `Failed to associate portal window with parent window`, so the chooser isn't attached to the VectorCraft window as its parent.

**Workaround:** raise Hyprland's `misc:anr_missed_pings`, or click Wait.

title: Feature request: Scale Artwork with Artboard when resizing artboards
author: AutoHenry
body:
## Summary
Illustrator has a **Scale Artwork with Artboard** option: when an artboard is resized, the art on it scales proportionally with it. VectorCraft doesn't have this yet. Resizing an artboard (Artboard Options, the Artboard tool's handles, Transform panel W/H) only changes the artboard's rectangle and leaves the art as it was.

## Current behaviour (main, after v0.3.1)
- `artboard.setProps` replaces `rect` and name only; art is never touched on a resize.
- **Move Artwork with Artboard** (`moveArt`) exists for move, copy, duplicate and Rearrange, but it only translates.
- Fit to Artwork Bounds / Fit to Selected Art go the other way (artboard to art).

## Proposed
- An option **Scale Artwork with Artboard** in Artboard Options, the Artboard tool's options/Control bar and the Properties panel, alongside Move Artwork with Artboard.
- When on, art fully inside the artboard (the same set `artboard_art` gathers for `moveArt`, locked/hidden per `moveLockedWithArtboard`) is scaled from the artboard's reference point by the width and height ratio.
- Respect the Scale Strokes & Effects and Scale Corners preferences, as the Scale transform does.
- Artboard guides scale/move with it.
- One undo step.
- Over MCP: `scaleArt?: bool` on `artboard.setProps` (and the tool resize), returning the ids scaled.

## Why
Common when repurposing a design to a new size (A4 to A5, social formats, icon sizes). Without it the workaround is select all on the artboard, scale with a computed percentage, then realign to the artboard.

DesignCraft already has the equivalent (Adjust Layout / Liquid Layout on page resize).

title: Type: kinsoku level and the opening bracket at a paragraph's start — which settings and defaults?
author: imachus
body:
Two more pieces of Japanese composition where the behaviour is clear from JLREQ but the *setting* is a design choice, so I'd like to ask before writing them (as with #432).

## 1. Kinsoku level

**Today:** one kinsoku set (`no_line_start` / `no_line_end` in `crates/text/src/shape.rs`). Besides closing brackets and punctuation, it also keeps 々 (cl-09), ー (cl-10) and small kana (cl-11) from starting a line.

**JLREQ** Appendix C.3 (https://www.w3.org/TR/jlreq/#addendum_a3) lists four levels of line-breaking rules:
- Level 1, Very loose (newspapers)
- Level 2, Loose (magazines)
- Level 3, **Strict (Default, general publications)**: allows a break before 々, the prolonged sound mark (cl-10) and small kana (cl-11).
- Level 4, Very strict: no exceptions to its Table 2.

So today's set keeps characters off the line start that JLREQ's default level allows there. The classes are in §3.1.7 (https://www.w3.org/TR/jlreq/#characters_not_starting_a_line).

**Options I see:**
1. A paragraph attribute with JLREQ's four levels (Paragraph panel and `text.setFormat {kinsoku}`). New type would take level 3, and existing documents would keep today's set (only written when set, like `mojikumi`).
2. Two levels only (today's set and JLREQ level 3).
3. Keep one set and only change it to level 3.

## 2. An opening bracket at the start of a paragraph

**Today** (with Line-end Punctuation Half Width): an opening bracket starting a *wrapped* line is set flush (#417). At the *start of a paragraph* it keeps its full width, so its face sits half an em in, after any first-line indent.

**JLREQ** §3.1.5 (https://www.w3.org/TR/jlreq/#positioning_of_opening_brackets_at_line_head) describes three patterns, assuming a one-em first-line indent:
- ① The first line is indented one em before the bracket's face, and wrapped lines start flush (tentsuki).
- ② The first line is indented one and a half ems, and wrapped lines half an em.
- ③ The first line is indented half an em, and wrapped lines start flush.

title: Illustrator EPS and .ai import: read layers, hidden objects and hidden text from the editing data
author: DisasterAreaDesigns
body:
## The problem

Illustrator-saved EPS files are my working format: my printer only accepts EPS. I have a large archive of them, organised by layer, and I need to open them, edit them and save them again with the structure intact.

Today an EPS comes in as its printed page: one layer, and nothing that was hidden. Re-saving it loses the layer names, their order, hidden layers, hidden objects and hidden text. A PDF-compatible `.ai` comes in with layers, but with art and type that differ from the original.

An Illustrator EPS is a flattened PostScript page. After `%%EOF` it carries an editing copy of the document in `%AI9_PrivateDataBegin/End` (Zstandard-compressed `%AI24_DataStream`, or zlib `%AI9_DataStream` in older files). A `.ai` has the same data in `/PieceInfo/Illustrator/Private`.

## What I built

A local branch with one commit, written with Claude Code. I haven't pushed it anywhere yet; I can open a PR from a fork once there is a yes.

- **Editing-copy reader** (`crates/eps/src/import/native.rs`): layers, sublayers, groups, compound paths, clip groups, hidden objects and custom colours, run by the existing PostScript interpreter through a small prologue. It falls back to the page, with a warning, when a shown layer uses an operator it doesn't read, or when the art differs from the page by more than 5%.
- **Text document reader** (`ate.rs`): type on hidden layers and hidden objects has no page copy, so its content and position come from the file's text document. Shown type keeps the page's own text objects. Area type and type on a path are left out with a note.
- **`.ai`** goes through the same reader, so the layer rules match.
- **Overwrite guard:** a file whose import left things out isn't written over unless asked (`acknowledgeLoss`, CLI `--replace-lossy`).
- **Font fix:** font names with a re-encoding suffix (`Name*1`) now resolve to their family. This was why one of my fonts was never found.
- Pure Rust (`ruzstd`), wasm builds, importers are fuzzed, es/it/…

title: Layer panel expands all groups on file load, causing severe UI slowdowns with complex files

body:
When opening large vector projects (e.g., a ~50MB file containing extensive layer structures, groups, linework vectors, and blob brush color masks), VectorCraft automatically expands/unwraps all groups and folders in the Layer panel by default.

This causes two primary issues:

1.    Performance Bottleneck: The UI framerate drops significantly while all these groups remain expanded in the panel. Performance instantly recovers to smooth, normal levels as soon as the groups/folders are manually collapsed one by one.

2.    User Experience / Workflow Issue: Unlike standard vector software like Adobe Illustrator, layer folder expansion states are not preserved. Having every group forcefully expanded upon opening a file clutters the UI and requires repetitive manual collapsing in every session.

Suggested Improvements:

Preserve / Control Expansion States: Retain the user's explicit folder collapse/expand states across sessions, or keep groups collapsed by default when opening a file (similar to Adobe Illustrator).

Layer Panel Rendering Optimization: Investigate why rendering expanded tree structures in the Layer panel introduces such a heavy performance overhead on large object counts.

Steps to Reproduce:

1 - Open a large vector file (>50MB) containing numerous nested groups and vector elements.

2 - Observe that the Layer panel automatically expands all groups/folders.

3 - Notice the UI framerate drop and lag when interacting with the canvas/interface.

4 - Manually collapse the expanded groups in the Layer panel.

5 - Observe that normal UI performance and framerate are instantly restored.

title: ArtCraft Canvas monorepo
author: Haven-King
body:
# ArtCraft Canvas monorepo

This is a bigger topic and discussion than I think is suitable for the Discord server, and I chose to open the issue here rather than the PhotoCraft repository because (A) it's less busy and less likely to get lost and (B) DesignCraft seems to be effectively forked off of VectorCraft, and thus this repository acts as a reasonable place for a decision about both.

## Summary

Merge VectorCraft, PhotoCraft, DesignCraft and PdfCraft into one Cargo workspace in a new repository, `storytold/artcraft-canvas`. Each app keeps its own directory, version and roadmap. Code the apps share moves into a common set of core crates, one crate per PR, after the move.

## Motivation

The four apps were started from the same template and copied code between them. The copies have since drifted. Today a fix or feature written for one app must be ported by hand to the others, or it isn't ported at all.

### Goals

1. **Less duplicate code and effort.** Write geometry, color management, commands, undo, the panic guard, the control channel, MCP, theming, preferences and xtask once.
2. **Features every app inherits.** A change to a shared crate reaches all apps in one PR. Examples:

title: Artboard tool: Delete/Backspace don't delete the active artboard (fix included)
author: mateususa
body:
## Bug

With the Artboard tool (Shift+O), clicking an artboard and pressing **Delete** or **Backspace** does nothing, even when the document has more than one artboard. The trash button in **Window › Artboards** does delete it.

Found while using a local Windows build at `b73e19ee`.

## Cause

`ArtboardTool::key` (`crates/tools/src/xform/artboard.rs`) handles Delete/Backspace, but the tool never overrides `Tool::claims_key`, which returns `false` by default. `crates/ui-egui/src/shortcuts.rs` only hands Delete/Backspace to a tool that claims them, so the keypress goes to the Clear shortcut instead. Clear deletes selected objects and leaves the artboard alone.

Gradient, Puppet Warp and Slice already claim their keys this way. The existing tests call `ArtboardTool::key` / `Session::tool_key` directly, which bypasses the routing, so they didn't catch it.

## Suggested fix

The tool claims Delete/Backspace while no drag is in progress and more than one artboard exists. With only one artboard left (it can't be deleted), the keys stay with the shortcut, as before. `key()` checks the same condition, so the two can't drift apart.

```diff
diff --git a/crates/engine/src/tests_xform.rs b/crates/engine/src/tests_xform.rs
index e790a65b..524adf23 100644
--- a/crates/engine/src/tests_xform.rs
+++ b/crates/engine/src/tests_xform.rs
@@ -247,10 +247,13 @@ fn artboard_tool_moves_with_art_creates_and_deletes() {
     assert_eq!(s.doc().unwrap().doc.artboards.len(), 2);
     assert_eq!(s.tool_options()["active"], 1);
     assert_eq!(s.doc().unwrap().doc.artboards[1].rect, Rect::new(1000.0, 0.0, 1200.0, 100.0));
-    // Delete it.
+    // Delete it: the tool takes the key ahead of the Clear shortcut (the UI only hands Delete to a
+    // tool that claims it).
+    assert!(s.tool_claims_key(ToolKey::Delete, ViewInfo::default()));
     s.tool_key(ToolKey::Delete, Mods::default(), ViewInfo::default()).unwrap();
     assert_eq!(s.doc().unwrap().doc.artboards.len(), 1);

title: Affinity export: write .af documents that Affinity opens
author: callmeBalloch
body:
Native Affinity import landed in #667 (PhotoCraft: storytold/photocraft#1607; see also storytold/photocraft#1126). Writing Affinity files is not implemented. It needs:

- A writer for the container (header, `#FAT`/`#FT2` tables, zlib/zstd entries, CRCs, the `Thmb` preview record) and the object stream in `doc.dat`, with the version, class and field tags Affinity expects.
- A decision on what is written:
  - our own layers mapped back to Affinity's;
  - unknown records from an imported file carried through unchanged (a round trip);
  - or a minimal document that Affinity is known to accept.
- **Validation in Affinity itself.** Every file written must be opened in Affinity 2 and 3, on macOS and Windows, compared against our render, and saved again by Affinity. No contributor on this has had an Affinity installation so far. Until someone can run those checks, export stays "unsupported": shipping files nobody has opened in Affinity would risk users' work.

The synthetic containers in the engine tests are test fixtures that our reader accepts, not an exporter: Affinity has never opened them.

title: Affinity import: effects, adjustments, brushes, master pages and other remaining gaps
author: callmeBalloch
body:
Native import (#667) reports each of these in the import warning, but doesn't import them yet. They are listed roughly by how often the 176 public sample documents hit them:

- [ ] Layer effects (shadows, glows, outlines, bevels…) and live filters.
- [ ] Adjustment layers.
- [ ] Brush and pressure strokes (imported as plain strokes).
- [ ] Master pages and their instances (Publisher).
- [ ] Symbols and embedded documents as live content (they come in as Affinity's cached picture).
- [ ] Special shapes: cloud, heart, cog, callouts, arrows… (imported as their bounding ellipse).
- [ ] Transparency gradients, fill opacity and bitmap fills.
- [ ] Conical gradients (imported as radial).
- [ ] Corner types other than round; stars with rounded points.
- [ ] Several fills or strokes on one object (one of each is used).
- [ ] Text: outlined or scaled text, fields (page numbers…), frames with columns or a curved outline.
- [ ] CMYK and Lab documents are converted without the document's colour profile.
- [ ] Blend modes VectorCraft lacks: Average, Negation, Reflect, Glow, Erase, Add, Linear Light….

Each item should come with a public, permissively licensed sample (added to the pinned corpus manifest) and a ceiling in the corpus test.

## Summary

**File → New from Template…** opens a file dialog aimed at `~/Documents/VectorCraft Templates`. On locales where the XDG documents folder is not named `Documents` (Italian: `Documenti`), and/or when the folder has never been created, the system dialog errors:

`templates_folder` in `crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/save.rs` builds `home/Documents/VectorCraft Templates` when the preference is empty. That path does not exist on this machine (`~/Documents` missing; `~/Documenti` has no `VectorCraft Templates` either).

title: Glyphs whose ToUnicode maps to U+FFFD render as "�" (digits lost in Illustrator .ai files)
author: netfox-web
body:
### Summary

When a PDF / PDF-compatible `.ai` file has a font whose `ToUnicode` CMap maps some glyphs to **U+FFFD**, VectorCraft draws those glyphs as `�`. MuPDF and Acrobat draw the correct glyphs, because the glyph outlines are embedded in the file.

We hit this with real Adobe Illustrator `.ai` files: every digit in the label text (sizes, phone numbers, dates, addresses) opened as `�`. In those files Illustrator wrote `<CID> <FFFD>` for the digit glyphs of an embedded CID-keyed CJK font (Source Han Sans TC Regular, `Identity-H`). Installing the font locally doesn't help, because the Unicode value is lost before the font is looked up.

### Environment

- VectorCraft 0.7.0, Windows x64 portable. 0.5.0 behaves the same.
- Reproduced with `vectorcraft-cli convert` and when opening the file in the app.

### Minimal reproduction (no customer content)

The script below generates `tounicode-fffd-digits.pdf`, about 210 KB. It embeds Source Sans 3 (OFL, from adobe-fonts/source-sans) as a Type0 / Identity-H font, writes three lines of text, and then rewrites the `ToUnicode` CMap so that only the digit glyphs map to `<FFFD>`. The other glyphs keep their real Unicode values.

```python
# pip install pymupdf ; put SourceSans3-Regular.otf next to this script
import re, pymupdf

doc = pymupdf.open(); pg = doc.new_page(width=300, height=130)
pg.insert_font(fontname="ss3", fontfile="SourceSans3-Regular.otf")
for i, s in enumerate(["Size 20.5x10.5x13cm", "Tel 02-12345678", "Date 2023.04.30"]):
    pg.insert_text((20, 40 + 30 * i), s, fontname="ss3", fontsize=16)
doc.save("_tmp.pdf"); doc.close()

d = pymupdf.open("_tmp.pdf")
for xref, *_ in d.get_page_fonts(0):
    m = re.search(r"/ToUnicode (\d+) 0 R", d.xref_object(xref))
    if not m: continue
    tx = int(m.group(1)); cm = d.xref_stream(tx).decode("latin1"); mp = {}
    for blk in re.findall(r"beginbfchar(.*?)endbfchar", cm, re.S):
        for a, b in re.findall(r"<([0-9A-Fa-f]+)>\s*<([0-9A-Fa-f]+)>", blk): mp[int(a, 16)] = b.…

title: Editing-data import (#637): Illustrator EPS renders drift, off-artboard art grows Fit to Artwork Bounds to metres
author: fastmikey99
body:
Running the editing-data import from #637 (as of `ec43ac5a` onwards, tested today) against a corpus of real-world print files (customer artwork, so I can't attach them). We open files headless with `document.open {textAs: "outlines"}`, then `artboard.fitToArt` and export, and compare renders against Ghostscript's render of the same file.

The good: the *"only the PDF-compatible part of this file was read"* warning is gone on 5 PDF-compatible `.ai` files, and nothing that opened before fails now.

Two regressions:

**1. Illustrator EPS renders drift from the page.** Three Illustrator-written EPS files (CS-era prolog, live text in Arial, fonts not embedded) that matched Ghostscript within 0.5–1.6% of pixels now differ by 20–64%. The new warning on all three is *"the text is on the layers in the order the page draws it…"*. On one, the art bounds after `fitToArt` went from 275 × 94 mm to 685 × 368 mm, so something off the page now comes in.

**2. Off-artboard art from the editing data reaches the document.** On two PDF-compatible `.ai` files, `fitToArt` now grows the artboard to 3.6–7 m (before: the page, 381 × 610 and 717 × 1576 mm). The editing data's art outside the artboards comes in as ordinary art, where the PDF part never drew it. New warnings on these: *"objects with several fills or strokes, effects…"* and *"the art on the layers differs from the file's…"*. Two more `.ai` files that clip to the page show 2–3× the pixel difference against Ghostscript (1.4% → 4.0%, 2.3% → 7.0%).

What would help us, either:
- a `document.open` option to choose the source, e.g. `source: "pdf" | "editing"` (today the editing data is used whenever it can be read), or
- art the editing data holds outside every artboard kept on a hidden, non-printing layer (as #419 does for art whose layer can't be told), so it neither shows nor counts in Fit to Artwork Bounds.

Happy to re-run the corpus against fixes and report numbers.

title: Which Rust version should cargo xtask ci run on? (no toolchain pinned; clippy 1.99 fails in affinity)
author: DisasterAreaDesigns
body:
Which Rust version should contributors run `cargo xtask ci` with? Should it be pinned?

While checking storytold/vectorcraft#762 I ran the full `cargo xtask ci` on current stable (rustc/clippy 1.99.0, 2026-09-28) and the `clippy` step fails on code the PR doesn't touch:

```
error: using `chunks_exact` with a constant chunk size   (clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks)
  crates/affinity/src/container.rs:340, container.rs:352, paint.rs:132, raster.rs:134
```

The gate stops at `clippy`, so `test`, `assets`, `brands`, `layers` and `wasm` don't run at all unless each is run by hand.

What I found about the toolchain:
- There is no `rust-toolchain(.toml)`.
- `Cargo.toml` has `rust-version = "1.95"`, which is the minimum supported version, not a lint baseline.
- The workflows in `.github/workflows` (`release`, `freebsd`, `windows7`, `windows-arm64`, `packaging-lint`) don't run `cargo xtask ci` or clippy, so nothing on GitHub says which version the gate is meant to pass on. `release.yml` uses `stable` and `windows7.yml` pins a nightly.

Questions:
1. Is there a Rust version `main` is expected to pass `cargo xtask ci` on (1.95? the previous stable?), and should it be pinned with a `rust-toolchain.toml`?
2. Or should the four `affinity` lints just be fixed with `as_chunks`, so the gate passes on the newest stable?

Happy to send a PR for either. Separately, `ui-egui`'s `dialogs::save_options::tests::save_a_copy_and_template_suggest_their_names` fails on `main` on macOS (the picker folder comes back `/` where the test expects `/templates`); I left that alone.

title: save_a_copy_and_template_suggest_their_names fails for any user who can't create /templates
author: DisasterAreaDesigns
body:
`dialogs::save_options::tests::save_a_copy_and_template_suggest_their_names` fails unless the tests run as a user who can create `/templates`

Follow-up to #767, as asked there. It fails on a clean `origin/main` (f837c930) with `cargo test -p vectorcraft-ui-egui --lib` on macOS, rustc 1.99.0, as a normal user:

```
---- dialogs::save_options::tests::save_a_copy_and_template_suggest_their_names stdout ----
thread '...' panicked at crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs/save_options.rs:341:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: ("Untitled-1 template.vctemplate", Some("/"))
 right: ("Untitled-1 template.vctemplate", Some("/templates"))
```

Cause: the test sets `prefs.templates_folder = "/templates"` (line 333) and expects the picker to start there. Since #703, `templates_dialog_folder` (`crates/engine/src/cmd/fileio/save.rs`) tries `create_dir_all` on the folder and, when that fails, starts the dialog in the nearest existing parent. A normal user can't create a folder in `/`, so the picker starts in `/`. This isn't specific to macOS: it should fail the same way on Linux and anywhere else the tests run as a non-root user. It only passes where `/` is writable (root, some containers), and there it leaves a `/templates` folder on the machine.

Suggested fix: make the test use a folder it owns, for example `std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("vc-templates-{}", std::process::id()))`, assert that folder is the picker's start, and remove it afterwards. I can send that as a PR if you'd like.

title: Illustrator guides / non-printing construction lines are lost on .ai import (dielines, registration frames)
author: netfox-web
body:
### Summary

Illustrator files often carry **non-printing construction lines**: ruler guides, path guides made with *View › Guides › Make Guides*, and non-printing layers. In packaging and print-and-cut work these lines are the die lines, fold lines and registration frames. VectorCraft drops all of them when it opens a `.ai` file, so the file looks complete but the dieline information is gone.

A related problem affects `.ai` files saved **without** "Create PDF Compatible File". These open as an empty artboard, and the only notice is the generic warning "only the PDF-compatible part of this file was read…".

### Environment

VectorCraft 0.7.0, Windows x64 portable.

### What we see (real customer files, which we can't share)

| | Adobe Illustrator | VectorCraft 0.7.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Envelope dieline file, PDF-compatible | Art plus cyan guide outlines and small registration frames | Art only. `guide.list` returns `[]`, and no guide paths are imported |
| Same kind of file saved without PDF compatibility | Full content | Empty artboard. `info.kinds` shows only `{'Layer': 2}` and the PNG export is blank |

In the second case the content does exist in the file. It is in the page's `/PieceInfo /Illustrator /Private /AIPrivateData1..N` streams, which hold `%AI12_CompressedData` plus zlib with `%AI5_FileFormat 10.0` (newer files use `%AI24_ZStandard_Data`). The PDF content stream is empty.

### Requests, in priority order

1. **Import guides.** Bring in ruler guides and path guides from the Illustrator private data, as VectorCraft `guide`s or as guide paths, so construction lines survive a round trip.
2. **Keep non-printing layers.** Keep the layer's *Print* flag rather than flattening or dropping the layer.
3. **Clearer diagnostics.** When the PDF-compatible part is empty but `AIPrivateData` exists, say so explicitly. For example: "This .ai was saved without PDF compatibility; N KB of Illustrator-native data was not imported. Re-save with 'Create PDF Compatible File' or…

title: .ai import: text glyphs whose subset code the file doesn't name import as outlined paths (one text object comes in split)
author: realjonnysax
body:
## What and why

Opening a PDF-compatible `.ai` whose text uses a subset font without a ToUnicode CMap: a glyph whose subset code can't be mapped back to Unicode is rejected by `type_glyph` and imports as the glyph's outlined paths, while the rest of the same text object imports as editable point type. One text object comes in split: editing the text leaves the unnamed glyph's outlines behind as art, and they don't move or reflow with it.

`type_glyph` (crates/pdf/src/import.rs) resolves a glyph's character three ways: the font's own mapping (`as_unicode`), Adobe's CID tables, then the character names in the font program. When all three fail it returns `false`, and the caller draws the glyph's outline as paths with the warning "text was converted to outlines" (import.rs:1597). A subset font without ToUnicode hits this on the first glyph the subset renumbered: Adobe's single-byte subset encoding renumbers glyphs into the control range (the first used glyph takes 0x1F) while codes that survive keep their ASCII values, so most characters resolve and the renumbered ones don't.

## Repro

Windows x64, VectorCraft v0.7.0:

1. Open a PDF-compatible `.ai` saved by Illustrator: text "RADA", LiebeLotte Regular 370.679 pt, white, letter-spacing 16.681, one line. (I can share the file.)
2. The PDF content stream draws the text as one op of 4 glyphs, single-byte subset encoding: `1F 41 44 41` (R, A, D, A). The file carries no ToUnicode CMap, so R (code 0x1F) has no mapping the importer can find.
3. `vectorcraft-cli info` reports: fonts - LiebeLotte, `missing: false`, `status: "exact"`; kinds - 17 Path, 1 Type; warnings - "text was converted to outlines".
4. The import is one Type object reading "ADA" and the R as outlined paths. A render draws all four letters (the R's outline path is correct), so the page looks right; the R just isn't type.

(The file's text stroke, which Illustrator expanded to paths in the PDF, also comes in as paths - that part is the file's, not this bug.)

title: Type set in an older installed version of a font can't be matched (only one version per family and style is kept)
author: jmverges
body:
**What happens**
A font library can hold two versions of one family and style, e.g. a current `Montserrat-Bold.ttf` beside an old `montserrat.ttf` whose family and style are also "Montserrat Bold". A PDF/`.ai` whose type was set in the old one opens with that type as outlines ("text whose glyphs differ from the installed font of the same name was kept as outlines"), even though the matching font is installed. With only the old file installed, the same file opens as editable type.

**Why**
- `FontDb::add_font_from` skips a face whose family and style are already loaded, so the second version never loads.
- `matching_face` (PDF import) tries the family's other styles, not other versions of the same style.
- `CharStyle` names a font by family and style only, so even a matched old version couldn't be drawn or edited in it afterwards.

**Proposal**
Keep every version (the first loaded stays the one family and style resolve to, so nothing changes for anyone else). Let import try the other versions, and let type name the version it was matched to with an optional `CharStyle` field (skipped when `None`, so existing documents and files are unchanged). PR to follow.

title: Image Trace: add photographs and scanned drawings to quality benchmarks
author: andeecollard
body:
## Request

Please add a representative corpus of photographs and scanned drawings for Image Trace quality benchmarks and regression tests.

The tracer is algorithmic, so this is a request for an evaluation corpus and quality-driven tuning, rather than a machine-learning training dataset. The existing synthetic tests cover useful geometric and correctness properties, but real images expose fragmentation, paper noise and loss of drawing detail that simple shapes do not capture.

## Motivation from local photo tests

We tested two 744 × 984 photographs (a hand and ivy) with the official 0.7.0 CLI and source commit cbacb47fdb0eb506022055be72f27caf4e776bc1. With colors=21, noise=12, paths=65, corners=60, method=abutting and ignoreWhite=false:

| Input | Paths | Anchors |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Hand photograph | 5,606 | 47,960 |
| Ivy photograph | 22,874 | 124,550 |

Rendered results looked fragmented, with many small regions. For these inputs and settings, the SVG and PNG outputs were byte-for-byte identical to our earlier 0.4.0 results. Raising only noise to 200 increased path counts to 7,378 and 31,172 respectively. This is an observation to investigate, not a claim that fewer paths are always better.

On the source commit above, changing the palette to Full Tone produced 4,745 paths / 27 colours for the hand and 60,600 paths / 144 colours for the ivy. It changed the tonal rendering but did not visibly resolve the fragmentation in our tests.

These are illustrative local measurements, not a reproducible public fixture submission: the photographs are not attached. We have not yet tested scanned drawings, but would like those included in the benchmark coverage too.

## Suggested coverage

- Photographs with smooth gradients, skin tones, foliage, fine texture and high-contrast edges.

title: Add a System theme option that follows the macOS light/dark appearance
author: coygeek
body:
## Summary

Add a System choice to VectorCraft's interface theme setting that follows the macOS light/dark appearance live, so the app changes with the rest of the desktop when macOS switches appearance automatically.

## Problem to solve

macOS can switch between Light and Dark appearance automatically (System Settings → Appearance → Auto changes it at sunset and sunrise), and many Mac apps offer a "System" theme choice that tracks it.

VectorCraft offers only manual interface brightness levels. VectorCraft → Appearance and Settings → User Interface → Brightness list "Dark", "Medium Dark" (the default), "Medium Light" and "Light", defined by `Brightness` in `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` and persisted in `ui.json`. Because VectorCraft only has manual choices, a user whose macOS appearance switches automatically has to change the app theme by hand at least twice a day, or leave it mismatched with every other app.

## Proposed behavior

Add System to the existing theme choice. With System selected, the app applies a light theme while macOS is in Light mode and a dark theme while it is in Dark mode, both at launch and immediately when the OS appearance changes while the app is open. The saved choice stays System; only the displayed theme changes. The existing manual choices keep working as they do today.

1. The theme control offers a System choice (for example "System" or "Use system setting") alongside the existing manual choices, and every place that exposes the theme (VectorCraft → Appearance and Settings → User Interface → Brightness) shows it.
